The Premier League is set to introduce a new LGBTQ+ inclusion campaign after ending its partnership with Stonewall, the charity behind the widely recognised Rainbow Laces initiative.

Stonewallâs Rainbow Laces campaign, introduced in 2013, became a fixture across English football, with players from all Premier League clubs wearing rainbow-coloured laces and captains donning rainbow armbands to promote acceptance and equality. The campaign aimed to support LGBTQ+ rights and foster inclusivity among fans and young people.

After over a decade of collaboration, the league will now lead its own campaign, timed to coincide with LGBTQ+ History Month in February, The Telegraph report.

"Rainbow Laces has benefited from a wide range of partners with a natural ebb and flow reflecting cultural and sporting changes," a Stonewall spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"Alongside other sporting bodies the FA has been instrumental in advancing LGBTQ+ inclusion at the grassroots level and more recently the Women's Super League has taken up the mantle as the women's game has grown - enabling Rainbow Laces to reach more diverse audiences.".

Despite Stonewall's efforts, recent reports from Kick It Out reveal an alarming increase in discriminatory incidents in football, including rises in sexism, transphobia and faith-based abuse, with racism continuing to be the most prevalent issue.

Sources indicate that controversies around playersâ attitudes to rainbow armbands have also made headlines. Last season, Ipswich captain Sam Morsy declined to wear one due to religious beliefs, while Crystal Palaceâs Marc GuÃ©hi faced criticism for personalising his armband with the phrase âI Love Jesus.â.

Additionally, Manchester United scrapped looks for LGBTQ+ support jackets after a player refused to participate.

With no openly gay or bisexual players right now in the Premier League, and the surge in discriminatory incidents, some question the timing of the split from Stonewall â an organisation highly respected for its work in LGBTQ+ advocacy.

Details of the Premier Leagueâs new campaign are still under wraps, but as the league presses âreset,â thereâs hope it will introduce a meaningful and effective initiative that advances equality rather than undermines it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, this Christmas, Everton in the Community is calling on supporters to help tackle loneliness and bring the true Christmas Spirit of the Blues to those who need it most. Loneliness can affect anyone, at any time of the year. It could be an older person facing another Christmas without their loved ones, a young person struggling to find where they belong, a parent finding it difficult to cope or someone surrounded by people but still feeling alone. That's why the official charitable arm of Everton Football Club is launching Christmas Spirit of the Blues, a campaign dedicated to raising awareness of loneliness in all its forms and ensuring everyone knows there is somewhere they can turn. Dedicated to breaking down barriers and supporting its local community since 1988, Everton in the Community delivers more than 50 inclusive, free programmes, each designed to tackle different societal challenges. From supporting young people back into education and giving latest fathers access to vital support networks, to helping military veterans navigate life after the forces, each programme shares the same ambition - to improve confidence, provide a sense of belonging and remind people just how crucial they are. To launch the campaign, Everton in the Community brought together participants, staff, supporters and players past and present at Hill Dickinson Stadium for a special performance of the iconic Liverpool Express hit, Spirit of the Blues. Liverpool-based brass band Allerton Brass performed a slowed-down version of the track, creating a poignant moment of togetherness and highlighting the power of music to bring people together. Throughout the build-up to Christmas, the campaign will shine a light on the experiences of people who have faced loneliness and explore how finding support, friendship and a sense of belonging has made a difference to their lives. Among those sharing their stories is Gina, who has found cherished friendships through Everton in the Community's Stand Together programme following the loss of her husband, and a young man whose experience of loneliness brought him to the brink of suicide. The campaign will also hear from father-of-two Sean, who reached out to Everton in the Community in the middle of the night after his wife tragically died just 12 hours after giving birth to their second son. “My newborn baby and his two-year-old brother were asleep, and I found myself feeling completely alone, drowning in grief and crying uncontrollably. “It was a hail Mary. I just needed to reach out to someone and, as an Evertonian, I knew about Everton in the Community – but I didn't expect the level of help I did get. It was a lifesaver.”  At a time when his world had been turned upside down, Sean indicates reaching out gave him someone to turn to when he felt he had nowhere else to go, and marked the first step towards navigating life without his wife. Dan Halliday, Head of Fundraising at Everton in the Community, noted: “For thousands of people across the Liverpool City Region and beyond, loneliness, social isolation and grief can feel even heavier at Christmas. “The pressure to feel happy or the absence of familiar handwriting on a Christmas card can be painful reminders of what's missing. “This Christmas, a donation to Everton in the Community could help someone feel seen, supported and part of something bigger. Together, we can make sure nobody has to face loneliness alone.”  To donate to Everton in the Community and join our mission to end loneliness together, visit (insert link). For more information about accessing support, visit https://www.evertoninthecommunity.org/projects/minds/accessing-mental-health-support/.

This Christmas, Everton in the Community is calling on supporters to help tackle loneliness and bring the true Christmas Spirit of the Blues to those who need it most.

Loneliness can affect anyone, at any time of the year. It could be an older person facing another Christmas without their loved ones, a young person struggling to find where they belong, a parent finding it difficult to cope or someone surrounded by people but still feeling alone.

That's why the official charitable arm of Everton Football Club is launching Christmas Spirit of the Blues, a campaign dedicated to raising awareness of loneliness in all its forms and ensuring everyone knows there is somewhere they can turn.

Dedicated to breaking down barriers and supporting its local community since 1988, Everton in the Community delivers more than 50 inclusive, free programmes, each designed to tackle different societal challenges.

From supporting young people back into education and giving newly introduced fathers access to vital support networks, to helping military veterans navigate life after the forces, each programme shares the same ambition - to improve confidence, provide a sense of belonging and remind people just how important they are.

To launch the campaign, Everton in the Community brought together participants, staff, supporters and players past and present at Hill Dickinson Stadium for a special performance of the iconic Liverpool Express hit, Spirit of the Blues.

Liverpool-based brass band Allerton Brass performed a slowed-down version of the track, creating a poignant moment of togetherness and highlighting the power of music to bring people together.

Throughout the build-up to Christmas, the campaign will shine a light on the experiences of people who have faced loneliness and explore how finding support, friendship and a sense of belonging has made a difference to their lives.

Among those sharing their stories is Gina, who has found cherished friendships through Everton in the Community's Stand Together programme following the loss of her husband, and a young man whose experience of loneliness brought him to the brink of suicide.

The campaign will also hear from father-of-two Sean, who reached out to Everton in the Community in the middle of the night after his wife tragically died just 12 hours after giving birth to their second son.

“My newborn baby and his two-year-old brother were asleep, and I found myself feeling completely alone, drowning in grief and crying uncontrollably.

Sources indicate that “It was a hail Mary. I just needed to reach out to someone and, as an Evertonian, I knew about Everton in the Community – but I didn't expect the level of help I did get. It was a lifesaver.”.

At a time when his world had been turned upside down, Sean indicates reaching out gave him someone to turn to when he felt he had nowhere else to go, and marked the first step towards navigating life without his wife.

Dan Halliday, Head of Fundraising at Everton in the Community, remarked: “For thousands of people across the Liverpool City Region and beyond, loneliness, social isolation and grief can feel even heavier at Christmas.

“The pressure to feel happy or the absence of familiar handwriting on a Christmas card can be painful reminders of what's missing.

“This Christmas, a donation to Everton in the Community could help someone feel seen, supported and part of something bigger. Together, we can make sure nobody has to face loneliness alone.”.

To donate to Everton in the Community and join our mission to end loneliness together, visit (insert link).

For more information about accessing support, visit https://www.evertoninthecommunity.org/projects/minds/accessing-mental-health-support/.

London’s people-first approach to smart-city development

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (890 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A virtual-reality model of London’s main financial district, the City of London, has mapped the size and location of every building.Credit: Mike Kemp/In Pictures via Getty Images.
  • Recent findings suggest that london has risen to fourth place in the IMD Smart City Index 2026, up from sixth place in 2025 and eighth place in 2024.
  • In a recent development, “We increasingly describe our work as ‘city innovation’ rather than ‘smart cities’, because in many people’s minds ‘smart’ is associated with gadgets and gizmos,” states Dorling.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A virtual-reality model of London’s main financial district, the City of London, has mapped the size and location of every building.Credit: Mike Kemp/In Pictures via Getty Images.

Recent findings suggest that london has risen to fourth place in the IMD Smart City Index 2026, up from sixth place in 2025 and eighth place in 2024. The index — which is published by IMD, an independent Swiss business institute — draws mostly on residents’ perceptions of infrastructure and technology, not a tally of sensors. That focus on perspective is important, says Trevor Dorling, managing director of DG Cities, a private urban-innovation consultancy spun out of the Royal Borough of Greenwich local authority, which works to make better use of data and introduce latest technologies in the southeast London borough.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

In a recent development, “We increasingly describe our work as ‘city innovation’ rather than ‘smart cities’, because in many people’s minds ‘smart’ is associated with gadgets and gizmos,” states Dorling. “The aim is to use technology to create better places for people. It shouldn’t be the technologists who define what ‘better’ is, but the communities that live there.”.

Recent findings suggest that there is plenty of evidence that London has the resources and knowledge to apply research solutions in such a people-centred way. In the 2026 Nature Index Science Cities table, London is ranked 21st overall, but it jumps to 5th place for health-sciences output, for instance.

The Smart Mobility Living Lab, created by a consortium of public and private organizations, including DG Cities, spans 24 kilometres of roads in Greenwich and the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park in Stratford, and is one example of London’s efforts to create societal impact with its innovation.

The area has more than 1,000 different road features, from speed bumps and pedestrian crossings to one-way systems and bridges, that allow companies to test new vehicles and services in busy, real-world complexity. “The driving force for this was the rapid development of self-driving technologies and exploring the opportunities this presented for safety and accessibility, as well as the challenges,” says Dorling.

Trials to test self-driving shuttle buses and delivery vans have put the technology in public view, with residents invited to ride in the test vehicles, an openness that Dorling says has helped overcome scepticism and brought local authorities into the development process at an early stage.

London’s digital-twin projects are similarly pragmatic. The local authority in Harrow (northwest London) uses high-resolution drone imagery to inspect and measure roofs and buildings remotely and to build interactive maps of parks. The council used this approach in April 2026 to make a 3D model of Headstone Manor and Museum — a restored medieval complex and local-history museum — saving £12,000 (US$16,260) by avoiding a conventional roof survey with scaffolding and manual inspections.

In London’s main financial district, known as the City of London, a virtual-reality model created by the local authority in collaboration with researchers and digital spatial mappers has captured the size and location of every building, window, lamppost and traffic light within the area to within two centimetres of accuracy, allowing planners and the public to properly scrutinize building proposals.

Elsa Arcaute, a complexity science researcher at University College London, cautions against too much faith in digital twins, as a city with all its complexity and interplay between urbanity, nature and human behaviour cannot be completely duplicated.

Italy legend Fabio Cannavaro admits Zinedine Zidane’s headbutt in the 2006 World Cup Final helped him win the Ballon d’Or: ‘It’s worth three times more now; I don’t see how a defender can win it again.’.

The legendary defender won the Ballon d’Or 20 years ago today. Cannavaro, currently the Uzbekistan national team coach, remains the last defender and the last Italian player to have won the coveted award.

“Now it’s worth three times more. No defender has won it since, and I don’t see how it can happen again,” he told Gazzetta.

When the journalist argued that Pau Cubarsì might be the closest, Cannavaro replied.

“A Barcelona defender—the city that criticised my victory the most.”.

Catalan newspapers strongly criticised Cannavaro’s Ballon d’Or win 20 years ago, arguing that Barcelona striker Samuel Eto’o deserved it more.

Recent findings suggest that “Criticism has never annoyed me. Now I smile. It seems that it is my fault if Maldini, Baresi or Cubarsì have never won it,” Cannavaro replied.

The former defender revealed how he learned he had won the Ballon d’Or.

Industry observers note that “I remember a France Football journalist stopped me in front of the Real Madrid training centre. He got into my car and noted: ‘I must tell you something: Buffon can’t reach you; you have won, and we must do an interview.’ I thought: ‘Is this a joke?’ When I watch games of that season, I think: ‘Mamma mia! I was playing so well.’ But I knew, as I know today, that if Zidane had not given that headbutt, it would have been much more complicated.”.

Cannavaro was named the best player in the world in 2006 after helping Italy win the World Cup that year.

The Final against France was one of the most epic games ever and saw Zidane sent off in extra time for headbutting Italy defender Marco Materazzi.

That Final remains Italy’s last World Cup knockout game. What should Italian football do, especially defensively, to return to greatness?

“We’ve only stopped working on individual technique, on running, and on the habit of defending with the ball frontally and laterally,” Cannavaro replied.

“Each role has its characteristics, and sometimes they prefer a goalkeeper who can make a 70-meter pass to one who actually makes saves. It’s okay, but then don’t complain if he concedes at an important moment.”.

According to recent reports, when asked whether his mentality has changed now that he has become a coach, Cannavaro replied: “For sure. When you start a coaching career, you think your ideas are the most notable in the world; then you understand you have to adapt. I’ve seen coaches sacked because they wanted to change the team’s menu or train in the morning instead of the afternoon. Let’s say that I’ve become wiser and more experienced.”.

During the same interview, the former Juventus, Napoli, Parma and Inter defender remarked Liverpool defender Virgil Van Dijk told him during the 2026 World Cup that he’d like to play in Serie A one day.

#220597. Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1089 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1089 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • During talks on ending the war in Ukraine, Russian representatives in Abu Dhabi presented a document containing far-reaching demands, The Newly introduced York Times reports.
  • Dated November 10, the document reportedly calls not only for an end to Western arms deliveries to Ukraine but also for NATO to withdraw its troops and bases and move them back to where they were in 1997.
  • Recent findings suggest that the year 1997 refers to the NATO alliance before its first eastward expansion, according to the Kremlin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During talks on ending the war in Ukraine, Russian representatives in Abu Dhabi presented a document containing far-reaching demands, The Newly introduced York Times reports.

Dated November 10, the document reportedly calls not only for an end to Western arms deliveries to Ukraine but also for NATO to withdraw its troops and bases and move them back to where they were in 1997.

Recent findings suggest that the year 1997 refers to the NATO alliance before its first eastward expansion, according to the Kremlin. At the time, NATO had 16 members. Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary had already been invited to join but did not formally become members of the defense alliance until two years later. In the following years, more countries in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe joined, followed most recently by countries in Scandinavia. Today, NATO has 32 member states in Europe and North America.

According to the report, Russia is not explicitly demanding that Central and Eastern European countries leave, but rather that the NATO alliance end its military presence in those countries.

According to recent reports, A withdrawal of NATO troops and bases from member states that joined the alliance after 1997 would significantly weaken their defense capabilities. For example, since 2004, NATO allies, including Germany, have taken turns policing the airspace over Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

Because the Baltic states do not have fighter jets of their own for independent air policing, NATO provides the capability. Since 2026, the mission has been part of a broader air defense presence. The planned deployment of the German Lithuania Brigade, which is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2027, would also have to be halted.

In Romania, meanwhile, the Mihail Kogalniceanu Air Base near Constanța on the Black Sea is at the moment being expanded. Once completed, it is set to become Europe's largest NATO air base by area — even larger than Ramstein in Germany.

"Under no circumstances will we allow anyone to establish new security rules for this part of the world over the heads of Poland and Europe," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told TVP World. His Bulgarian counterpart, Rumen Radev, called a NATO withdrawal "unthinkable and unrealistic." No country should be forced by external pressure to reverse its decision on which alliance to join.

Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal also rejected any Russian say in changes to Europe's security order: "We have nothing to discuss with Russia about Europe's security order; it is working well.".

The strong rejection from the capitals of NATO's eastern members, however, masks fears along the alliance's eastern flank that a deal between Washington and Moscow could turn their security into a bargaining chip.

In the event of an armed attack on a NATO member, the other alliance members are obligated under Article 5 to come to its aid. Each member decides for itself what measures it considers necessary, which may include the use of military force.

It has been revealed that for the mutual defense commitment to deter a potential aggressor, that country must believe NATO can intervene militarily rapidly and effectively in a crisis. The deployment of allied troops along the eastern flank serves precisely this purpose. A withdrawal would make defense more difficult and could lead Russia to believe that an attack on NATO territory would involve fewer risks for Moscow.

Sources indicate that as part of their security framework, European countries have agreed that states are free to decide which alliances they wish to join. NATO points to Article 10 of its founding treaty, which enshrines its open-door policy for European countries. The 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act also explicitly stated that neither side had the right to veto the other's decisions.

Back in November 1990, the participating states of the Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe (CSCE), including the Soviet Union, had already agreed in the Charter of Paris to respect each country's freedom to choose its own security arrangements.

During the negotiations surrounding German reunification, then-US Secretary of State James Baker and German Foreign Minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher used language that suggested putting limits on NATO's eastward expansion.

Their remarks came during discussions about unified Germany's membership in NATO and the possible deployment of NATO forces on the territory of the former East Germany. However, no written, legally binding general promise was ever agreed that NATO would never expand to include other former Warsaw Pact countries.

According to recent reports, in the 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act, both sides declared that they no longer considered each other adversaries. NATO stated that, under the security conditions prevailing at the time and in the foreseeable future, it intended to ensure its collective defense through reinforcement rather than the additional permanent stationing of "substantial combat forces." The agreement explicitly gave Moscow no veto over NATO decisions.

According to recent reports, in the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, Russia, the United States and the United Kingdom reaffirmed their commitment to respect Ukraine's independence and existing borders and to refrain from the use of force. These assurances were linked to Ukraine's decision to give up its nuclear weapons. However, the memorandum did not oblige the United States or the United Kingdom to defend Ukraine militarily in the event of an attack. NATO membership was not addressed at the time.

Industry observers note that just over two months before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the Kremlin presented two draft treaties to the United States and NATO. In them, Russia demanded an end to further NATO enlargement. The draft agreement with NATO also proposed that Russia and NATO members that had already joined the alliance as of May 27, 1997, refrain from deploying additional troops or weapons on the territory of other European countries beyond the levels stationed there on that date.

In a recent development, security guarantees for the postwar period and a future security framework for Europe were also on the agenda in Abu Dhabi. Negotiating NATO troop deployments and alliance enlargement alongside an end to the war in Ukraine would give Moscow additional leverage. Russia has long maintained that the "root causes" of the war must be addressed. The Kremlin includes NATO enlargement and the alliance's military presence in Eastern Europe among those causes.

So far, no significant Western player has expressed willingness to accept Russia's demands in Abu Dhabi. On the contrary, former Polish intelligence coordinator Stanislaw Zaryn viewed the talks as an attempt to buy time and weaken the West ahead of another confrontation.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Hundreds of delegates gathered at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Wednesday as the waterfront venue hosted the launch of a upcoming guide setting the standard for the provision of accessible experiences when attending live sport.
  • Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition will serve as a blueprint for venue operators, governing bodies, designers and others involved in stadium development on how to deliver accessible experiences for disabled supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hundreds of delegates gathered at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Wednesday as the waterfront venue hosted the launch of a latest guide setting the standard for the provision of accessible experiences when attending live sport. Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition will serve as a blueprint for venue operators, governing bodies, designers and others involved in stadium development on how to deliver accessible experiences for disabled supporters. Disabled sports broadcaster Andy Stevenson hosted the event, with executives from both Level Playing Field and the Equality and Human Rights Commission addressing attendees. Panel discussions also allowed for insight from industry experts and disabled supporters to be shared with officials from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media & Sport, the Sports Grounds Safety Authority and governing bodies across a range of sports. Everton officials and members of Everton Disabled Supporters' Association (EDSA) were among representatives of disabled supporter groups, clubs and venues from across the country. Christopher Massam, Accessibility Lead at Everton Football Club, said: "We are truly honoured to host the launch of Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and to bring together so many great minds and voices on what is a vitally vital subject. "As a Club, we have worked closely with Level Playing Field and EDSA for a number of years as part of our efforts to continually appraise and enhance the accessibility provision across all our stadiums and sites. "Accessibility and inclusivity were key factors in the design of Hill Dickinson Stadium and, since its opening, we have continued to learn from feedback and refine our offering to create the best possible experience for all our supporters and visitors. "Hosting an event like today's allows us to share work we are incredibly proud of, but also to strengthen our relationships with key stakeholders, with supporter groups and to continue that learning journey."Chair of Level Playing Field, Tony Taylor, said: “Today marks an important milestone, as we strive to make attending live sport genuinely accessible for all disabled fans. “It has been our pleasure to lead on this project and channel the input from different stakeholders to define a set of standards and outline a roadmap to deliver access and inclusion. “Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition has the potential to make a dramatic difference to the experiences of so many disabled supporters, and it is important that we all come together to realise this opportunity.” Hill Dickinson Stadium, officially opened in August 2025, offers more wheelchair bays than any other English club stadium and accessible viewing platforms located on multiples levels. The stadium is also equipped with a state-of-the-art sensory room, quiet rooms, Changing Places facilities and low-level counters, as well as providing step-free access to all concourse levels. In addition to hosting Premier League matches, the stadium has become an established home for international football, rugby league and rugby union. To learn more about accessibility provision at Hill Dickinson Stadium, click here. Further details about the Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and how to access the guide, can be found at levelplayingfield.org.uk.

Hundreds of delegates gathered at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Wednesday as the waterfront venue hosted the launch of a upcoming guide setting the standard for the provision of accessible experiences when attending live sport.

Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition will serve as a blueprint for venue operators, governing bodies, designers and others involved in stadium development on how to deliver accessible experiences for disabled supporters.

Disabled sports broadcaster Andy Stevenson hosted the event, with executives from both Level Playing Field and the Equality and Human Rights Commission addressing attendees.

Panel discussions also allowed for insight from industry experts and disabled supporters to be shared with officials from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media & Sport, the Sports Grounds Safety Authority and governing bodies across a range of sports.

Everton officials and members of Everton Disabled Supporters' Association (EDSA) were among representatives of disabled supporter groups, clubs and venues from across the country.

Christopher Massam, Accessibility Lead at Everton Football Club, said: "We are truly honoured to host the launch of Level Playing Field's Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and to bring together so many great minds and voices on what is a vitally key subject.

"As a Club, we have worked closely with Level Playing Field and EDSA for a number of years as part of our efforts to continually appraise and enhance the accessibility provision across all our stadiums and sites.

"Accessibility and inclusivity were key factors in the design of Hill Dickinson Stadium and, since its opening, we have continued to learn from feedback and refine our offering to create the best possible experience for all our supporters and visitors.

"Hosting an event like today's allows us to share work we are incredibly proud of, but also to strengthen our relationships with key stakeholders, with supporter groups and to continue that learning journey.".

Chair of Level Playing Field, Tony Taylor, remarked: “Today marks an key milestone, as we strive to make attending live sport genuinely accessible for all disabled fans.

“It has been our pleasure to lead on this project and channel the input from different stakeholders to define a set of standards and outline a roadmap to deliver access and inclusion.

“Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition has the potential to make a dramatic difference to the experiences of so many disabled supporters, and it is crucial that we all come together to realise this opportunity.”.

Hill Dickinson Stadium, officially opened in August 2025, offers more wheelchair bays than any other English club stadium and accessible viewing platforms located on multiples levels.

The stadium is also equipped with a state-of-the-art sensory room, quiet rooms, Changing Places facilities and low-level counters, as well as providing step-free access to all concourse levels.

In addition to hosting Premier League matches, the stadium has become an established home for international football, rugby league and rugby union.

To learn more about accessibility provision at Hill Dickinson Stadium, click here.

Further details about the Accessible Stadia 2nd Edition and how to access the guide, can be found at levelplayingfield.org.uk.

‘There were some games in the past where we went (away to substantial teams) and you're not sure you can really do it,’ Gross tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘But we should now have a mindset that we can win every game. I really believe in that. We have the players. That’s what I said.

‘People say we are nice club and, yeah, maybe we are. But on the pitch, it was time to be ruthless. Time to kill games, be a big club. That’s what this is about now.’.

Brighton sit second in the Premier League table, despite a disappointment at Hull last weekend that saw them lose a game they had dominated at the death. Gross, 35, ended that one on his knees in his own penalty area, having tried in vain to stop Oli McBurnie sliding in Hull’s second goal.

‘That felt really, really bad,’ he says. ‘Maybe today (Tuesday) is the first day I am starting to feel a bit better about it. I would be more worried if we didn’t create chances. We did. We just didn’t score.’.

Industry observers note that ‘On the pitch, it was time to be ruthless,' Pascal Gross tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Time to kill games, be a substantial club. That’s what this is about now’.

Brighton sit second in the Premier League table, despite a disappointment at Hull last weekend that saw them lose a game they had dominated at the death.

Before Gross returned for his second spell at Brighton last January, he sat down for a rather frank conversation with manager Fabian Hurzeler.

Brighton are six points behind leaders Arsenal – who they have already beaten 3-0 at the Amex – but are the Premier League’s top scorers by a distance, with 26.

Gross, the German who returned to Sussex after a short spell at Borussia Dortmund, has created an astonishing 31 chances for his team. That puts him only two behind the best in the country this term, his friend and Germany team-mate Florian Wirtz.

Industry observers note that the debate about Wirtz’s value or otherwise to Liverpool has swirled around the country since he arrived at Liverpool in the summer of 2025 for £116million. The conversation even reached Brighton’s training ground.

‘Jamie Redknapp was there and he asked me all about it just a couple weeks ago,’ Gross explains. ‘I just told him: "He's too good not to prove himself." People here still don't know how good he is, but they will. He's a complete package and he knows I support him a lot.

‘Football is a team sport. It’s not ever on one person. Also, nobody should forget just how difficult and different the Premier League is when you first come.’.

According to recent reports, gross knows this well. He smiles at the mention of his own first English away game – a 2-0 defeat at Leicester in August 2017 that brings to mind the Patrice Evra quote about his first experience of playing in England being akin to ‘an afternoon spent in a washing machine’.

Industry observers note that ‘I was on the floor so much that day that I looked like a little child,’ Gross recalls. ‘It was just all too physical. I knew I had to improve fast, play faster. My decision-making had to be quicker.

Recent findings suggest that ‘My father called me after and said I wouldn’t last three weeks if I played like that again. But I already knew. Going home that day, I really questioned a lot of things. But that’s just how hard it is when you come to the Premier League.’.

Gross had a brutal introduction to the Premier League in 2017, but it was a reminder of the level he needed to reach.

Recent findings suggest that gross fires in Brighton's equaliser at Old Trafford in the Carabao Cup back in September. The Seagulls trailed 2-0 but fought back brilliantly to dump out Man United.

Brighton players Luka Vuskovic and Groß visit local independent restaurant Riddle & Finns to support American Express' Shop Small campaign.

In a recent development, the Hull game was Gross' 300th in a Brighton shirt, and he is perhaps playing at a higher level than ever with four goals and four assists in the first 11 league games this season, as well as a goal in the Carabao Cup win at Manchester United. On an official club podcast, former striker and team-mate Glenn Murray labelled him Brighton's best-ever player, and last week he signed a new contract keeping him on the south coast until the end of next season.

Signed by Chris Hughton from Bundesliga side Ingolstadt after the Seagulls' promotion to the top division a little over nine years ago, Gross has had an inside view of the most successful period in the club’s history.

Industry observers note that during his time, Brighton have sold enough players for massive profit to make a pretty good Premier League XI – Robert Sanchez, Ben White, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marc Cucurella, Moises Caicedo, Alexis Mac Allister, Leandro Trossard and Joao Pedro get you most of the way there, for a total transfer taking of £424m. Gross suspects there will be more over time.

Equally, he feels the days of players using Brighton as a stepping stone to the next level are gone. A lack of commitment soon gets sniffed out, he states.

Recent findings suggest that ‘There have been players who saw it like that,’ he explains. ‘And they couldn't even get in our team because they came with the wrong mindset. If you don't have the right mentality, you don't want to work every day, you can't get in the Brighton team.

‘And if you do come with the right mentality and you push every day, and the team is doing well, I always say that good things will come for everybody – for the club, for the coaches, for the players.

It has been revealed that ‘I love the club, and we have major potential. There will always be players that move on. But I think the players who come here now, they know we are bigger than a jumping club. We're a big club in the Premier League. We have been there almost 10 years and are improving all the time.’.

Gross thought hard before first leaving Germany for England. He visited Brighton’s training ground twice before making his decision and, once he had, dug down into the individual statistics of the players who would soon be team-mates.

Gross (right) has seen a huge change at Brighton since joining from Bundesliga side Ingolstadt, where he played under former Southampton manager Ralph Hasenhuttl (left).

Brighton's form this season has been inspired by a prolific attack, with their 26 Premier League goals by far the most in the division.

They have progressed season on season despite the departure of a host of star players for major money, including Alexis Mac Allister (right) to Liverpool for £35m in 2023.

Industry observers note that having married and had two children in Sussex, Gross has the club in his heart and soul now. We meet to talk at beachfront restaurant Riddle & Finns as part of American Express’s Shop Small campaign, encouraging people to support local business.

During his spell at Dortmund – who he adored as a boy – Gross watched every Brighton game on TV. But it may not have been this way. There was a time, in pre-season 2020, when former Brighton manager Graham Potter told Gross he could leave.

It has been revealed that ‘That was hard to take,’ Gross says. ‘I asked him if there was no chance at all of me playing. I needed to know if he saw me as, like, No17 or 18 in the squad so that whatever I did, I wouldn't play. Or in his mind was I 12, 13 or 14?

Sources indicate that ‘Then I figured I could work my way back into the team because I would always back myself to prove the manager wrong. We lost a lot of games and eventually, I came back into the team.’.

Gross’s approach back then was to train as well and as hard as he could. Murray recalls that his attitude stood out.

‘It wasn’t my team-mates’ fault I wasn’t playing,’ explains Gross. ‘Why would I take it out on them? That wouldn’t make sense.’.

Culture is often discussed in modern football but it’s just a fresh word for an old truth: unhappy football teams tend to fail.

Sources indicate that ‘There are days when you see, maybe, that the way we play gives an opponent frustration and you can see bad body language,’ Gross says. ‘That's where I sense we have them.

It has been revealed that ‘It wasn’t my team-mates’ fault I wasn’t playing,’ explains Gross, pictured celebrating the win at Man City with Jack Hinshelwood. ‘Why would I take it out on them? That wouldn’t make sense’.

'If you don't have the right mentality, you don't want to work every day, you can't get in the Brighton team'.

According to recent reports, 'Players who come here now, they know we are bigger than a jumping club. We're a significant club in the Premier League'.

‘But there are also teams who maybe struggle but they are still together and they're still fighting and you see a group of guys who can still be hard to beat. That’s about culture. It’s notable and I think we value that here.’.

Recent findings suggest that as part of Brighton’s leadership group, Gross speaks regularly to manager and compatriot Hurzeler. His personal creed is that confidence should never bleed into arrogance – ‘I just hate that’ – and he believes that Hurzeler, known to rub the occasional manager up the wrong way, is on the right side of the line.

‘He is pushing, pushing,’ Gross says with a smile. ‘He has so much passion for the job, he puts so much work into it. He wants to challenge, he wants to think differently.

‘He doesn't want to think: “Everything is nice." He really wants to push himself and us. And that balance is a really fine balance. He's trying to stretch the limit and I think that's good.’.

Italy have been knocked out of the Nations League group phase, so when is their next match?

The last international games of the year were played during the November break, so Italy, like most other countries worldwide, will return to action next year, precisely in March.

The Azzurri finished third in their Nations League group, seeing winners France and runners-up Belgium progress to the quarter-finals.

Despite the disappointment of the elimination, which experts at BetPanda had widely predicted, it is fair to say the Azzurri must see the glass half full.

Their Nations League campaign featured victories over Turkiye and France, and only their two losses to Belgium sealed the Nazionale’s elimination.

Italy, however, still managed to secure a spot among the seeded teams in the Euro 2028 qualifying draw thanks to their Nations League results.

As previously mentioned, the next international break is in March 2027, running from Monday 22 to Tuesday 30. As the Azzurri won’t be playing in the Nations League quarter-finals, they’ll start their Euro 2028 qualifying campaign straight away.

In a recent development, italy will learn their opponents on December 6, when the qualifying draw takes place. The first match will be played on March 26, 2027 and the second on March 29. The Azzurri will likely be placed in one of the four-team qualifying groups after their elimination from the Nations League.

Regardless of their opponents, the Azzurri will look to start their qualification campaign strongly and bounce back after a 4-1 loss to Belgium in their most recent match.

“These nights can happen in the growth process; you need to learn from these experiences. Considering the way we got here, we had the chance to qualify, but we knew it would be tough, as Belgium are a strong team,” Mancini said at full time in Belgium.

“We are sad, but this night will help us going forward.”.

He has grabbed three wins, one draw and two defeats in his first six games in charge in his second spell. The Euro 2020 winner has signed a contract until 2030, when, hopefully, he’ll bring the Nazionale back to the World Cup.

Italy already know that their captain Gianluigi Donnarumma will miss the next international match after being booked in the most recent match against Belgium.

Gigio was one yellow card away from suspension prior to the game in Belgium, so he’ll miss the next one.

Predictably, Manchester City will replace the star with either Guglielmo Vicario (Juventus) or Marco Carnesecchi (Atalanta). The latter has recently suffered a knee injury, forcing him to undergo surgery, and the date of his return to action remains uncertain.

Man Utd show fight on night of chaos to give Carrick a glimpse of hope

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 34 min read (6894 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~34 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?
  • At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.
  • In a recent development, roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?

At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.

In a recent development, roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford. A fifth defeat in six matches and the club’s longest winless run for 48 years beckoned. It was toxic on and off the pitch.

And then something changed. United, from being a dishevelled, disorganised mess, suddenly seemed to remember who they were supposed to be and what they were supposed to represent. Surrender gave way to fight. A team that had been feeling sorry for themselves discovered some pride. A crowd that had been baying for blood turned Old Trafford into a bear pit of a very different kind, and Roma simply did not know what had hit them.

This club have served up some famous comebacks over the decades, but it was hard to think of too many occasions when the mood and momentum had shifted this violently from one half to the next.

Industry observers note that united fans were in open revolt in that first half, releasing green and gold balloons in protests before kick-off and then throwing tennis balls on to the pitch amid furious chanting against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The players looked like they would rather have been anywhere else.

And yet by the 86th minute Matheus Cunha’s wild celebrations were encapsulating a wild night, the Brazilian ripping off his shirt after his dramatic winner before launching himself into a delirious crowd drunk on the euphoria of a victory that had seemed improbable in the extreme at the interval, when boos cascaded from the stands.

Whether this proves little more than a thrilling, heroic interlude in the endgame for Carrick, or the start of a genuine turnaround, is hard to know. And, let’s be clear, there was so much about the first-half performance to concern the hierarchy, who came under persistent, furious attack from fans at war with an ownership it reviles and wants gone.

But the second half stood firmly at odds with the shambolic display that had preceded it and suggested all may not be quite lost just yet.

Aston Villa visit Old Trafford on Sunday in the final game before the international break and, if Carrick can follow this with another win, then it will be intriguing to see where the Old Trafford board goes from there.

Carrick may at least have been encouraged by some of the things Bruno Fernandes said after the game, not least that he warranted being dropped against Bournemouth. And it was the captain who kick-started the fightback against Roma, albeit at the second attempt.

In a recent development, he had won the penalty after being fouled by Gianluca Mancini only to then contrive to miss it. But a retake was ordered for encroachment and, given a second bite at the cherry, Fernandes made no mistake.

NO MISTAKE THIS TIME 💪 Bruno Fernandes gets United back in it after a penalty retake 😤 https://t.co/uQdkNs0lXo.

When Carlos Baleba pulled up with a hamstring injury within seconds of the restart as he burst into the penalty area, Carrick must have wondered what else could go wrong.

But as United went hell for leather, the home supporters who had spent much of the first half attacking the owners and staging a number of colourful protest acts, suddenly found their voice in a very different way.

According to recent reports, from being an atmosphere in which the players clearly felt cowed, Old Trafford was now rallying behind its men in red – and it helped to shake Roma in the process. They had been such good value for their lead, but now they were rocking, and United smelled blood.

There was wave after wave of attack as Roma desperately and often frantically tried to defend their goal, and it took a bad mistake from Leonardo Balerdi, who swung at thin air from Fernandes’s cross and missed the ball, to hand Cunha the chance to equalise.

IT'S 2-2! 💥 Cunha levels it up for United! 🔴🇧🇷 https://t.co/q60oQUoat1.

According to recent reports, at that point, the momentum was firmly in United’s favour and three minutes later they were in front. It is a source of bemusement among fans that Shea Lacey has not had more game-time considering how poor some senior players have been. And his arrival as a substitute made a big difference.

In a recent development, it was Lacey who speared an inch-perfect pass into Cunha, who turned sharply before drilling a stunning finish in off the near post. Cue bedlam.

MAN UNITED HAVE TURNED IT AROUND!!! 🔴🔥 From 2-0 down, to 3-2 up at Old Trafford 🤩 https://t.co/ATD8wDlc1e.

Cunha was booked for taking off his shirt as he crowd-surfed bear-chested among the fans and was then sent off minutes later after a poor challenge. A fittingly chaotic end to a crazy night for the match-winner.

Industry observers note that the difference to those opening 45 minutes was as stark as it gets. Indeed, the first half felt like a continuation from the fans of their blood-letting against Bournemouth.

When the clock hit 20.05 – a nod to the year 2005 when the Glazers bought the club – a pile of tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch from the Stretford End amid chants of “We Want Glazers Out”. They were promptly followed by cries of “Just like the Glazers, Jim Ratcliffe’s a c---” and “sell the club and f--- off home”.

Jason Wilcox, the club’s director of football, again copped for it. A banner read: “For the love, not the ‘likes’”. When the Champions League music played, hundreds of green and gold balloons – a reference to the club’s original colours and the 2010 protest movement – were released.

Sources indicate that on the pitch, United were all over the place. Carrick had dropped Lisandro Martínez after his red card against Chelsea but his replacement Ayden Heaven was at fault for the first goal after getting sucked in and failing to check his shoulder. Had he done, he would have seen Matías Soulé unmarked and in acres of space with Diogo Dalot, United’s left-back, caught high up the pitch. Soulé made no mistake with his finish.

THAT DIDN'T TAKE LONG 😬 United fall behind after just 11 minutes as Roma score through Matías Soulé 🇦🇷 https://t.co/DtIOFJYZ6D.

Heaven almost did the same again soon after before more blunders handed Roma a second. Soulé tried to find Donyell Malen with a pass but miscued to Harry Maguire. Yet the England defender then proceeded to give the ball straight back to Soulé, who turned Dalot and shot with Heaven blocking the ball with his right arm as he lunged to stop the effort. Malen continued his rich scoring vein from the penalty spot.

Malen makes it TWO-NIL ROMA from the spot, after a handball from Heaven in the box 😬 https://t.co/kUeOeQNRES.

Industry observers note that at that point, no one could have reckoned on the comeback that followed. Where it leads, who knows.

Speaking after the match, Michael Carrick was very positive about his side’s performance.

In a recent development, “It was a good night. I have to a lot of credit to the players for starters, showing that character and that quality when we needed it and to the supporters. This place does incredible, magical things,” stated Carrick.

In a recent development, “I thought we grew into it the first half  after giving the goals too easily. We spoke at half time about how this place can change, it only takes one moment and it certainly did that and the boys made the most of every opportunity and were fantastic in the end.”.

It has been revealed that asked about how he inspired the team at half-time he kept it simple: “Just not to get too disappointed about things. I thought we were coming into the game, getting around their box and it didn’t feel that way to the players because they were carrying too much frustration and disappointment and I knew we were doing some good things in the game against a really good team.

“Playing against man-to-man as much as they are, you probably get more failure than success and it’s still being positive and the boys responded so well to that.”.

As for whether this will change United’s momentum now, he was cautious not to get carried away.

“Listen it’s one game. It depends on what happens next and we’ve got to capitalise on that but tonight the boys indicated an awful lot,” he said.

“And I thought we came out the second half, unfortunately with Carlos having to go off and Youri coming on the pitch and I thought he was fantastic, he revealed everything that he is as a personality, as a character and with his experience to step in the game like that, and the boys just went with the flow and you could feel how positive it was and it was nice to see this place like that again.”.

Captain Bruno Fernandes also spoke after the match, acknowledging the difficulties the team has faced.

In a recent development, “It’s tough to say something at the moment to be honest. It’s been a tough period for us, we have not been able to play in the way we want, get the results we want. We’ve done some good bits, but not had the consistency to do it through a whole game to get results and it’s been tough.

Sources indicate that “But today was important to get a win. We knew after that we still had the fans with us, we felt we could change it with a goal and something and fortunately we did it today.”.

As for his penalty miss and re-take: “First one didn’t go the way I wanted, I did something wrong but I got a second chance and I cleared my head and my mind was only on to get the ball in back of the net.

“It’s been tough for the fans, we understand that. Having that belief from their side helps the team a lot and today was one of those days that Old Trafford came alive.”.

After his first start as he returns from injury, Kobbie Mainoo was full of praise for the fans, saying he cherished the relationship the team had with them.

“It’s unlike anything else. We’d do anything for these fans on the pitch, all the love they give us throughout the season it’s only right we repay them and it’s a bit of fun just jumping into the stands with them.”.

Speaking to Amazon after the match, Youri Tielemans said: “There has been a lot of pressure on him [Carrick] and that’s how we repay him, with a comeback like this, big character, big fight.”.

Sources indicate that “We just kept working, we kept believing. We were on the front foot in the second half, we tried to push them into their goal and we succeeded.”.

As for whether or not the performance would be enough to keep Carrick in his role at United: “That’s a different question. The only thing we can do is stick behind him, fight for him and fight for the club.

“At the end of the day we are on the pitch and we need to show what we are capable of and tonight, especially in the second half, we demonstrated what we can do and we turned up the gears.

“Let’s hope this is a good turnaround for us and let’s hope we can build on this.”.

For the badge ✊🇾🇪 https://t.co/BOGdZRmkiZ.

“Great credit to Michael Carrick because they were down and out at half-time. They were everywhere in that first-half, and he had to change and tweak things,” Alan Shearer remarked after the final whistle.

“I noted what can he do, I didn’t know where he would start, and he must have started in the dressing room, and pointing at a few people telling them to be brave and courageous and move the ball quicker, and run in behind and they did all those things in the second half and got their reward by getting their win.”.

Possession: United 52% vs 48% Roma.

Touches in opposition box: 30 vs 8.

For the first time in months, United fans have witnessed a performance worth cheering (at least in the second half).

Industry observers note that as Michael Carrick led his players around the pitch – with the occasional smile and fist pump – they were all greeted by cheers and applause in the stands. Some of them might have forgotten what that was like.

It has been revealed that MAN UNITED HAVE TURNED IT AROUND!!! 🔴🔥 From 2-0 down, to 3-2 up at Old Trafford 🤩 https://t.co/ATD8wDlc1e.

There is no guarantee that this is enough to keep Michael Carrick in a job beyond the November international break, but if he keeps his role, this will certainly be a turning point.

We will have to wait until Amazon release their All or Nothing documentary to find out what he said to them in the dressing room at half time but whatever it was, it worked.

Manchester United finally have their win!

Final seconds and Roma are pushing for an equaliser. Pisilli sends a cross in but Yoro heads it away.

Roma come again, but Mount wellies it half the length of the pitch to huge cheers.

The United team that went into the dressing room at half time did not look like they had a second half like this in them.

In a recent development, they almost throw it away as Cristante loops a ball into the box for Castro to head, but the striker connects poorly and sends it wide. He was also offside anyway.

Well Cunha has absolutely lost his head there. Booked for taking his shirt off just minutes ago, he goes in for a ridiculous late challenge and wipes out Balerdi. The ref rapidly produces a yellow and Cunha is off!

United will have to see out the final minutes with 10 men.

This is the energy that United have been looking for over the last few months, and wouldn’t you know that they’re about to reap the rewards.

IT'S 2-2! 💥 Cunha levels it up for United! 🔴🇧🇷 https://t.co/q60oQUoat1.

Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire come off, replaced by Mason Mount and Matthias de Ligt.

Probbably around six minutes to go here with the added time.

Incredible strike from Mateus Cunha to complete an astonishing second-half performance!

He picks up the ball from Lacey as he dashes into the box and looks up to see just a whisker of space at the near post and puts his foot through the ball!

He then takes of his shirt and launches himself into the crowd...

United have easily had the better of the second half and could take something from this.

Industry observers note that maguire goes down under pressure by Castro and tries to shield the ball and ends up in a tussle with the Roma striker. No cards given luckily for Maguire.

It has been revealed that and a bit of luck finally goes United’s way! A defensive blunder from Roma as Bruno Fernandes curls a ball into the box and Balerdi completely misses the ball as he tries to clear it from the box. Cunha is lurking behind him and turns the ball into the next low from close range.

Yoro passes the ball in to Mainoo on the edge of the area and he tries a back-heel, but there is no team-mate there to meet it and Roma bring the ball out again.

United intercept in midfield again, which is where the game has turned in the second half and they come again.

Sources indicate that 10 minutes plus added time left. United are still fighting for an equaliser here to their credit, but waiting until they were two goals down to start battling made it very hard for them.

Another Roma change, and it’s Donyell Malen making way for Santiago Castro. He will end tonight with just the one goal.

Seconds after stepping on the pitch, he gets in a tangle with Maguire and the England defender gets booked for bringing him dowm.

Cunha has a powerful attempt that’s parried away by Vásquez and collected by Lacey.

Plenty of shouts for a foul as he tries to cross the ball in, but the referee is unmoved to give a penalty.

It’s Ayden Heaven that makes way for Lisandro Martínez, while Amad Diallo comes off for Shea Lacey.

Roma making changes of their own. Mancini and Hermoso are replaced by Daniele Ghilardi and Evan Ndicka – two straight defensive swaps.

It has been revealed that yoro intercepts a ball in midfield and finds Bruno Fernandes. He tries to tee up Diallo but the winger loses the ball from another well-timed Roma challenge.

Tielemans tries to set Diallo free with a long ball but there’s too much on it and Vásquez comes to collect.

Roma trying again down but Cunha dispossesses Lulli, trying to release Bruno Fernandes. Lulli gets back to make the challenge and stop the run.

Industry observers note that cunha wins the ball and makes a run towards the box. He takes a shot but it is blocked on the edge of the area.

Mbeumo goes down off the ball, claiming a foul before Dalot also goes down in the box, looking for a penalty. The official is unmoved.

Fans are throwing objects onto the pitch from the Stretford End.

In the meantime, Rensch has been taken off, replaced by Emanuele Lulli.

According to recent reports, united fans are throwing tennis balls on the pitch and chanting “We want Glazers” out – the 20.05 minute protest in a nod to 2005, the year the Americans bought the club. “Sell United and f--- off home,” the Stretford End sings. Mayhem on and off the pitch.

Yellow cards for Bruno Fernandes and Matías Soulé as the two players exchange strong words and a shove.

Rensch went down and Roma players were screaming for the United players to put the ball out of play but they don’t.

Dalot caught in possession and the ball is picked off again. Roma make another run at goal and it’s blocked in the box but United are looking very shaky at the back.

And Donyell Malen makes it two!

He steps up to the spot and cool as you like send Lammens the wrong way to find the back of the net on the keeper’s right.

Malen makes it TWO-NIL ROMA from the spot, after a handball from Heaven in the box 😬 https://t.co/kUeOeQNRES.

United are in real trouble when they lose the ball. Again they are carved open and Mora takes the ball down the left, sending another looping ball across the field. Soulé tries to find Malen making the run in the box but he can’t quite reach it.

It rebounds at the feet of Soulé and Heaven concedes a penalty for a handball.

No shots or shots on target for United. One shot on target for Roma and one goal.

But Bruno Fernandes picks the ball up on the right wing from Diallo and fizzes a low ball across the face of goal. Mbeumo can’t quite connect and it is swept away from the feet of Cunha at the far post before he can tap it in.

This is obviously the last thing United would have wanted. The crowd – previously cheering every ball forward and every challenge – have gone quite quiet.

But just like that, Roma get the breakthrough.

United lose the ball and are carved open. Mora sends a long ball across the field and finds Soulé completely unmarked on the edge of the box. He brings it down, makes a short run and slots it past Lammens low at the near post.

THAT DIDN'T TAKE LONG 😬 United fall behind after just 11 minutes as Roma score through Matías Soulé 🇦🇷 https://t.co/DtIOFJYZ6D.

It has been revealed that mainoo sends a nice pass out to Diallo on the right who sends a ball to Bruno Fernandes on the overlap. His ball into the box is swiftly blocked but Mainoo has started very brightly and draws a foul in the next passage of play.

Bruno Fernandes sends a long ball downfield trying to set Mbeumo free but he can’t quite bring it down and control it, and Roma are back on the ball.

Not much in these early exchanges.

Cristante tries to slip a ball through to Malen in the centre of the box but it’s cleared away swiftly.

The Netherlands international picks up the ball again and is quickly swarmed before he can turn in the box. United staying disciplined so far.

Yoro wins the ball in midfield and United get a bit of possession up the field but a sloppy pass from Dalot gifts it back to Roma and now the visitors are probing the United final third.

But in great news for United, they have reached four minutes without conceding, which is a feat they had not achieved in their last two European games.

Lammens is not taking any chances playing out from the back though, opting for the long ball out every time.

Mainoo tries to lift a ball over the top from midfield for Diallo on the right-hand side, but he doesn’t quite get it right.

In a recent development, an early goal would definitely boost spirits here. United are enjoying a spell on the ball and that will suffice for now.

And we are underway in Old Trafford!

United need to get off to a steady start here, conceding an early goal could be devastating.

There’s a minute of silence before play in memory of Jesus de ​Miguel who died on Tuesday morning.

As the Champions League anthems plays, fans have released their yellow and green balloons from the stands in protest against the club’s owners.

A mix of boos and cheers from around the ground.

We are five minutes out and both teams are lined up in the tunnel.

One banner in the stands reads “We’ll support you evermore”.

We’re about to see what the players can muster to earn that support.

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a reminder of the teams taking to the field tonight:.

Man Utd XI (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Heaven; Baleba, Mainoo; Diallo, Cunha, Fernandes; Mbeumo.

Subs: Darlow, Heaton, Amass, De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui, Santos, Mount, T Fletcher, Tielemans, Lacey, Zirkzee.

AS Roma XI (3-4–2-1): Vazquez; Mancini, Balerdi, Hermoso; Rensch, Cristante, De Roon, Wesley; Soule, Rodrigo Mora; Malen.

Subs: De Marzi, Koulierakis, N’Dicka, Castro, Molina, Pisilli, Di Nunzio, Lulli, Ghilardi.

Bad timing with injuries means that tonight is the first time that Kobbie Mainoo and Carlos Baleba feature in midfield together.

Baleba was injured when he completed his £70m move from Brighton and Mainoo picked up his muscle injury as his team-mate returned to the substitutes bench.

It will be down to the two young players to stop Roma lacing balls through midfield to Malen and Carrick will need them to click on first time of trying.

Wayne Rooney has decided not to pull any punches tonight when it comes to his former club as he debates the possibility of a new manager arriving at Old Trafford.

“I’ll tell you Gabby with that group of players, none of the [possible replacement] managers are getting any more out of these players. The biggest job is getting them all out of the football club, that’s the biggest job,” he said to Gabby Logan.

The United manager has had his turn speaking to Amazon Prime with a very relaxed demeanour, despite the huge pressure sitting on his shoulders.

"It's a SIGNIFICANT night for us" 🗣️ Carrick gives his thoughts ahead of taking on Roma live on Prime 📺 https://t.co/BHFyKF4fXA.

The former Aston Villa striker has hit the ground running in his first full season with Roma, and has already raced to eight goals and an assist in nine Serie A matches. He notched 14 goals in 18 league matches in the second half of last season while on loan, and has picked up where he left off.

He’s already scored three in the Champions League, and could be looking eagerly at United’s shaky mentality to add to those numbers. He is the top scorer in Europe’s top five leagues in this calendar year, beating the likes of Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane.

Gasperini’s man-to-man style emphasises his skill in one-on-one situations, where his pace and drive with the ball make him a handful for even the best defenders.

Here is the full list of tonight’s fixtures:.

Matchday 4 is here ⚽️ #UCL https://t.co/tgJlzmaDAh.

Galatasaray are already 2-0 up on Stuttgart, while Sporting have found the breakthrough against Shakhtar Donetsk in the early kick-offs.

Manchester United fans are planning a series of in-stadium demonstrations at Old Trafford tonight in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s ownership.

Thousands of green and gold balloons – a nod to the club’s original colours as Newton Heath – are set to be released from the Stretford End when the Champions League music plays out ahead of kick-off.

There had been aims to bring a banner into the stadium bearing the words: “No newly introduced stadium, we want new owners” but that was blocked, apparently on the grounds of Uefa’s inability to sanction it in time.

The Glazers and Ratcliffe have come under growing attack this season with the club’s regular match going supporters at war with the owners.

A separate fans’ group has also been encouraging fans to join in anti Glazers and Ratcliffe chants in the 21st minute or, more specifically, after 20 minutes and 5 seconds: 20.05 is a nod to 2005, the year the Glazers completed their hostile takeover at Old Trafford.

It has been revealed that the main surprise for Roma is in goal, as with first-choice keeper Svilar out already, it has been confirmed that backup keeper Pierluigi Gollini has injured his back today. He has been replaced by Colombian Devis Vásquez in goal.

Roma: Vásquez; Balerdi, Mancini, Hermoso; Rensch, de Roon, Mora, Wesley; Soulé, Cristante; Malen.

Recent findings suggest that we have confirmation, Martínez is on the bench. He is replaced by Ayden Heaven while Bruno Fernandes is still with the captain’s armband in midfield. Kobbie Mainoo gets the nod as he returns from injury, along with Mateus Cunha and Mason Mount.

Your United team for tonight's #UCL clash 👊 https://t.co/TD9F6RjeAB.

Lisandro Martínez has been dropped by Michael Carrick in the wake of his red card madness against Chelsea.

The United manager has opted to pair Ayden Heaven in central defence with Harry Maguire for the Roma game with Martinez dropping to the bench.

The Argentina defender received a second yellow card for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face in Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea when he was also culpable for the first goal.

Martinez has been in dire form this season and was fined and publicly apologised after publicly criticising director of football Jason Wilcox and the Old Trafford board in the wake of the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid.

Kobbie Mainoo returns to midfield after missing the last four games through injury.

Ayden Heaven has just come out to speak with Prime Video, which has led Gabby Logan to assume that means that Lisandro Martínez will not start for Michael Carrick tonight.

Speaking with her, former United legend Wayne Rooney has noted the Argentine has “simply not been good enough” and should not necessarily feature again under Carrick.

When Alan Shearer was asked if he would include Martínez on a team sheet tonight, he did not mince his words, calling him a “liability”.

Ahead of the confirmed line-ups coming out shortly, there are certain players we know we will not be seeing today.

Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Luke Shaw (unspecified) and Benjamin Sesko (shin) remain sidelined for United, while Marcus Rashford and Amad Diallo will be assessed before the match.

There are no new concerns for Gasperini after his side’s latest match, the 5-2 win over Udinese, but he remains unable to select Muhammed Bah (ACL), Paulo Dybala, Manu Kone (thigh), Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) and first-choice keeper Mile Svilar (stress fracture, foot).

Happy Tuesday and thanks for tuning in to tonight’s coverage of Manchester United against Roma.

According to recent reports, it’s matchday four of the Champions League and Michael Carrick’s side host their Serie A opponents having failed to win any of their last nine matches across all competitions. Since their win against Sabah back in September (must feel like years ago to Carrick), they have suffered chastening defeats in Europe to Atlético Madrid and then Cesc Fabregas’s Como. This has been coupled with dismal performances in the Premier League, most recently a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Chelsea, where Lisandro Martínez was sent off for two ridiculous fouls.

Lisandro Martinez is shown a second yellow card following a VAR review 🟥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max ➡️https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/VLcAMNdqgZ.

All in all, there is the feeling that Carrick is simply a dead man walking, limping towards the international break after the United hierarchy decided on a stay of execution in their crisis talks earlier this month. If the beleaguered manager has any hope at all of hanging on to his job, he needs convincing results tonight and against Aston Villa on the weekend.

Despite the doom-mongering that circles the club, Carrick maintains that he has buried the hatchet with Bruno Fernandes following his captain’s public criticisms of the club, insisting that “the dressing room is a good place” in his pre-match press conference (more on that to come).

The visitors on the other hand, managed by Gian Piero Gasperini – who replaced Claudio Ranieri last summer – are certainly having a better time of it. They got off to a slow start in Europe, drawing with Fernebahce in their opening match but coming agonisingly close to stunning Real Madrid on matchday two at home. They went 3-1 up before three late goals snatched victory for Madrid.

Sources indicate that they bounced back with a convincing 4-0 win over Slovan Bratislava and their domestic campaign is off to an incredibly promising start. They are currently unbeaten in Serie A with seven wins and three draws. They sit third and are the highest scoring side, with 28 goals from their 10 games. Free-flowing though their attack is, there a certainly defensive frailties there to exploit as they conceded three in a six-goal thriller against Napoli, as well as two in both matches against Cagliari and Udinese.

It has been 19 years since Carrick was part of a United side that thrashed Roma 7-1 at Old Trafford, with the midfielder scoring two. Tonight he faces that same opponent with his job hanging by a thread and it remains to be seen if his team can produce any semblance of that spark to turn the tide. Feel free to drop us your score predictions in the comments – bragging rights on the line for the winner.

We’ll be bringing you team news, previews from the managers and more ahead of kick-off at 8pm!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan winger Diego Moreira infuriated Olympiacos fans and players with his goal celebration in a Europa League game in Athens, prompting Rossoneri coach Ruben Amorim to apologise at full time.

The incident happened in the final minutes of the game, after the Belgian winger scored to make it 4-2 for the Rossoneri.

La Gazzetta dello Sport describes what Moreira did to irritate the home fans and players.

The Belgian scored in front of the Greek supporters’ stand and stared at it, motionless, for a few seconds.

Safe to say that neither the home fans nor their players enjoyed the celebration, as Manolis Saliakas and João Silva confronted the Milan winger.

Silva wagged his finger at him, as to say: ‘You don’t do that in our house.’ A few seconds of tension followed. With Saliakas, there was a grim face-to-face that lasted a few seconds.

According to recent reports, “It won’t happen again. Moreira is a young lad who plays, but he has to grow,” Milan coach Amorim mentioned at full time.

Recent findings suggest that “We know we wouldn’t like it if they did that to our fans. It’s my responsibility, and I apologise, but he didn’t do it with bad intent.”.

Moreira has now scored five goals in 12 appearances across all competitions with Milan.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Helsinki Central Library Oodi is just one example of a building in the Finnish capital that uses real-time data to optimize energy efficiency.Credit: Sergei Gapon/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images.
  • Urban planners — and curious residents — can go online and click on almost any building in Helsinki to see a host of details including its age, height, heating source and estimated energy use.
  • Helsinki’s technical prowess in these kinds of projects is underpinned by a substantial research base; the city is ranked 100th among the world’s top 200 cities in the Nature Index, with particular strength in health sciences (ranked 69th), biological sciences (80th) and Earth and environmental sciences (83rd).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Helsinki Central Library Oodi is just one example of a building in the Finnish capital that uses real-time data to optimize energy efficiency.Credit: Sergei Gapon/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images.

Urban planners — and curious residents — can go online and click on almost any building in Helsinki to see a host of details including its age, height, heating source and estimated energy use. The information sits in the various maps that make up Helsinki 3D, an open-data digital twin of the city built by the City of Helsinki from aerial photographs, light and detection laser scanning (LiDAR) surveys, housing registers and geographical data. The project’s Energy and Climate Atlas estimates heating demand for nearly every building, models how it would change in response to different climate conditions and calculates the solar-panel potential across every roof and wall in the Finnish capital.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Helsinki’s technical prowess in these kinds of projects is underpinned by a substantial research base; the city is ranked 100th among the world’s top 200 cities in the Nature Index, with particular strength in health sciences (ranked 69th), biological sciences (80th) and Earth and environmental sciences (83rd). It produced 55% of Finland’s total Share in 2025, a ratio that is among the highest for cities in the overall top 200.

The city has treated itself as a laboratory, too. Kalasatama, a brownfield site in the harbour district of Helsinki, has been designated as an urban testbed for researchers, city officials and companies to try out novel urban infrastructure ideas.

Helsinki’s Nordic climate is also an advantage when it comes to handling the large amounts of data involved with smart cities. Cooler air reduces the energy needed to chill large data centres and the excess warmth created by such facilities is redirected to residents using heat pumps. One of the largest data-centre operators that publishes its waste heat recovery data says it recovers up to 90% of its waste heat, which is fed into the district heating network — enough to warm 14,000 two-room apartments.

One of Helsinki’s most distinct smart-city features is the way it uses data.

“We have to be responsible when we use AI. We must do it in a transparent way,” says Pasi Rautio, a service manager for the City of Helsinki’s AI and optimization unit.

The city’s AI register, for example, allows residents to keep tabs on AI projects the city’s government is running. It shows what data are being used and why, and offers the opportunity for public feedback.

Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
