📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life. A 10-game sample size -- that's the useful stuff. At this point, many but not all teams are what their analytics tell us they are. It's similar but not quite the same for players. Not many have hit the 900-minute mark yet, but plenty are at 500-plus, a body of evidence that usually isn't warped by any one good or bad game. Of course, it depends on how good or bad that game is.

Recent findings suggest that we are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions. We are, however, in a position to find some interesting questions. Here are five of them, in player form:.

Recent findings suggest that spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running. That's especially true when they're Bruno Guimaraes, terror of Premier League midfields in a Newcastle United shirt, a player who had long since seemed ready to step up to a Champions League contender. While it would be fair to say that the Brazilian's form is nothing like a problem for table-topping Arsenal, he has not exactly started like a house on fire. Mikel Arteta has acknowledged as much whenever he has spoken about Guimaraes, even when served up the opportunity to praise him after what seemed an impressive performance against Hull City.

"He's hitting serious levels now, but we can still take him to another level. That's my conviction; I told him that in the dressing room -- he owned a lot of moments in the game, but there is still much more to come." It would be fair to say that, Hull aside, the best levels he has hit have been as a substitute. When he comes off the bench, he passes more accurately, wins more tackles, creates chances and scores brilliant goals. As a starter, he has occasionally looked a beat off his teammates.

In a recent development, physical data from Gradient Sports hints as to what the concern might be. For every 90 Premier League minutes on the field, Guimaraes covers less of it at sprint speed (≥25 km/h) than any outfield player bar Mikel Merino and spends notably more time jogging than anyone, an average of 30 minutes. Compare Guimaraes to Declan Rice, an admittedly vertiginous bar, and it is easy to see why the newly introduced guy looks off the pace.

Equally, it explains why he's such a compelling substitute. When the other 21 players on the pitch are flagging, Guimaraes' comparative physical concerns go unexposed and he can run the show.

According to recent reports, that's all well and good for now, but he can't carry on like this, can he? You would have to assume that Myles Lewis-Skelly will have to make way even if the academy graduate's emergence as a midfield option unlocked an improved Declan Rice at the tail end of last season. The second most expensive signing in your history can't be an impact guy off the bench behind the homegrown kid, right? Probably not, but if there's any team that could justify the idea of Guimaraes as a 12th man, maybe it's Arsenal, where they pride themselves on their game-changing finishers.

Erling Haaland's Swiftian reign at the top of the Premier League xG chart has been interrupted, at least temporarily, by an unlikely source. You'd have to go back to the days of a marauding Romelu Lukaku for the last time an Everton striker looked like they might rule the roost. Only once since the Belgian's departure has an Evertonian cleared 20 goals in all competitions. In the last five, even a dozen has been beyond this club.

Thierno Barry isn't there yet, but boy is he on the right trajectory. His 7.28 non-penalty expected goals (npxG) puts him 0.22 ahead of Haaland and nearly 2.5 npxG up on anyone else in the league. Expand the pool to Europe's top five leagues and he is breathing rarefied air behind the top four of Lamine Yamal, Donyell Malen, Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe, all of whom have the advantage that they are not playing for an upper midtable outfit in the continent's most competitive division. And in that environment, Barry is making the hardest thing in the sport look easy: getting good shots in prime locations.

According to recent reports, if Barry were turning them in as often as he was getting them, Everton might be even higher than sixth. Still, six goals through 10 games is not to be sniffed at, particularly when the pressure on the 24-year-old was so intense. The bungling of a deadline-day move for Folarin Balogun, as Beto moved to Fiorentina, meant it was Barry or bust for David Moyes this season.

Perhaps it was an enforced show of faith for a player who was in and out of the XI last season, his first in England, that brought the best out of the former Villarreal man. His manager views the success in more straightforward terms. "He has settled down a bit more," remarked Moyes after Barry's brace helped down Coventry. "His language, his understanding, his communication is much better and he has worked hard to get himself in those positions to score.".

According to recent reports, it is easy to see why getting the soft factors right might have been all that was required. Barry is the ideal striker for the modern Premier League. Tall, strong and mobile -- he ranks third among center forwards for top speed this season, per Gradient Sports -- he can serve as an outball when a press needs beating and then get in the box. He might not have the technical elegance of an Mbappe, but he makes his presence felt and occupies high-value spaces. That is more valuable than it sounds, as proven when James Tarkowski's howitzer from range deflected in off him. You might not like it, but this is what elite center forward play looks like. Long may it continue, at least as far as Everton are concerned.

Industry observers note that there are three types of underrated footballers. First, your common-or-garden-variety underrated footballers, often to be found plying their trade at Wolverhampton Wanderers or Burnley. Ashley Westwood, in that season, put up stupidly high xA numbers. Then there are the so-often-dubbed-underrated that they actually become a bit overrated. Leighton Baines. Lee Carsley. They don't have to play for Everton, but it does help. Olivier Giroud is another. See, not all Everton.

Recent findings suggest that the most rarely spotted of the underrated is the chameleonic one, correctly pegged for a while, only to develop to the point that he is underrated in a completely different way to how he once was. Take Alex Iwobi. Some time ago, a consensus coalesced around the Nigeria international that he was a good player for a team at Fulham's level (and indeed Everton's). Any minute he was on the field, he would probably be delivering good performances for good Premier League teams.

Recent findings suggest that not anymore. Ten games in and Iwobi looks like one of the outstanding creative forces in the Premier League, critical to the march towards adequacy that Fulham have undertaken after a slow start to life with Alvaro Arbeloa.

Among true playmakers, Iwobi is one of the best at getting the ball into dangerous areas and creating for his teammates. Iwobi leads the league in expected assists with 2.95 and is tied with Bruno Fernandes for most passes completed into the penalty area. Only Pascal Gross has created more chances.

Recent findings suggest that those players can't match Iwobi when it comes to ball progression either. In terms of advancing the ball not just into the box but from deeper, Fulham's ball-playing fulcrum on the inside left channel has completed more progressive passes than anyone not named Declan Rice or Jan Paul van Hecke.

When Iwobi broke through at Arsenal, he displayed a preternatural sense for how to keep attacks alive, the pass before the pass before the pass. Now a 30-year-old, Iwobi still does that more than he unpicks defenses. One cannot argue, however, that he is not putting his teammates in the right spot. It is just that not everyone quite appreciates how often he does so just yet, including his own supporters, who jeered Iwobi when he was substituted in the early-season defeat to Crystal Palace. Since then, he has responded to his critics in style, teeing up two or more shots in each of Fulham's last seven Premier League matches. If a few more of them had been converted, in fact, if any of them had been converted, then Iwobi might not still be underrated.

The upper reaches of the list of most expensive transfers of all time are hardly all bangers all the time, but of the biggest money moves in the sport's history there are only a handful where at such an early stage you find yourself wondering if anyone really understood what the initiative was. Manchester City committed the best part of $150 million on Enzo Fernandez this summer, a fee only eclipsed by Neymar and Kylian Mbappe. Beyond a vague sense that it would be nice to give new manager Enzo Maresca one of his favorite players, what was it they had in mind?

Industry observers note that we pointed out earlier in the season that the aggressive positioning of Fernandez in the 5-3 win over Sunderland looked extreme; at the time it seemed reasonable to view it as a reflection of a stretched-out, chaotic game. Maresca had, of course, unlocked more number 10-ish qualities in the Argentine at Chelsea, but surely that had been reflective of what that team needed, particularly as Cole Palmer went off the boil? Perhaps not. Fernandez keeps popping up in the sort of positions that leave Elliot Anderson on an island. It is one thing to view Anderson as the latest Rodri, quite another to immediately throw the England international in at the deep end, tying a whole midfield together by force of will.

Sources indicate that of course you could sketch out a logic for why you might push Fernandez high. It is not so long ago that City deployed two playmakers in front of a sitting midfielder and they ruled the Premier League. Fernandez and Rayan Cherki aren't Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva though.

Industry observers note that maybe Cherki could be offering a level of creation on a par with City greats; he started well enough last season. In year two, he is creating lower-quality chances, his expected assists per 90 dropping by 50%, notably more than the slight uptick in the quality and quantity of shots he is taking. It's no surprise that Cherki is creating less when fewer of his touches are coming in the attacking third. The output has been there so far, five goals and two assists in nine Premier League games, but for that to continue, Maresca might want to be getting his No. 10 into more dangerous spots.

It has been revealed that instead, those seem to be going to Fernandez, who has not proven himself able to get the final-third production to justify his platforming. For every 100 touches he takes, he is delivering significantly less npxG+xA than in either of the previous two seasons. Meanwhile, he is less effective without the ball than he has been at any stage since coming to England. That's no wonder. If an opponent passes through City's frontline, then Fernandez does not have the mobility to get back.

Industry observers note that as such, to enable themselves to get perhaps a shot or two more than they would get with Ayyoub Bouaddi or Mateo Kovacic next to Anderson, City have made themselves an even more vulnerable side to the counterattack, already giving up more fast-break openings than they did in 2020-21 or 2021-22. Carry on like this, and Fernandez will become one of those nine-figure transfers, the ones that live in infamy.

In a recent development, it was a signing that delighted a city when it was unveiled in early August, and rightly so. Loaning Carl Rushworth from Brighton had been an inspired bit of business by Coventry City, the then-24-year-old goalkeeper anchoring the best defense in the division as Frank Lampard's side returned to the top flight for the first time in over a quarter of a century. A club-record £22 million fee seemed a snip for such a young talent.

In a recent development, all of that is worth bearing in mind given the struggles Rushworth has endured this season: saving just 53.7% of shots he has faced, conceding 5.19 more goals than the xG value of the shots he has faced. The swagger of last season has been replaced by a sloppiness apparent in both the goals he conceded in the second half against Tottenham, weak gloves doing nothing to repel efforts that came at him a bit quicker and a bit sooner than they might have last year.

None of this needs to be a problem for Rushworth. In 2023-24, James Trafford was another highly touted young goalkeeper afforded a shot at the big time by Burnley. He was obliterated up and down the Premier League, his first touch in the division picking the ball out of the net off Erling Haaland. Those struggles were the making of him, as they have broken others. It'll be some time yet before we discover which way these past few months send Rushworth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alphadjo Cissè already has 10 goals in his first four months at Milan, and on goals per minute he is ahead of Kylian Mbappé and Erling Haaland.

Recent findings suggest that as noted by Sky Sport Italia, the 20-year-old’s header against Olympiacos on Thursday took him into double figures for the season. He has six in Serie A and four in the Europa League, from just 15 appearances.

In a recent development, those numbers are even more impressive given how little he has played. He has started and completed the full 90 minutes only twice, and has played 782 minutes in total. That works out at a goal roughly every 78 minutes. He has also been ruthless in front of goal, converting 40% of his 25 shots.

Across all competitions in Europe, only Raphinha (a goal every 58.8 minutes) and Roma’s Donyell Malen (67.4) have a better rate. Cissè sits ahead of Mbappé (84.7), Haaland (95.7) and Lamine Yamal (111.2).

In Serie A alone, Malen is again the only forward ahead of him. Cissè’s rate of a goal every 74.3 minutes beats Lautaro Martínez (91.5), Francesco Pio Esposito (109.3) and Marcus Thuram (135.5).

He is also in form, having scored in three straight games against Genoa, Frosinone and Olympiacos.

His 10 goals already match Rafael Leão’s total for the whole of last season, which took the Portuguese 1,968 minutes. Cissè has done it in less than half that time.

Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The case ended without a verdict after both sides reached an out-of-court settlement.
  • In a recent development, as Zverev's lawyers noted in a statement sent to DW: "The criminal proceedings were discontinued...
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexander Zverev misrepresented the result of his 2024 domestic abuse trial, causing harm to his former partner and the mother of his child, Brenda Patea's lawyer has told DW.

The case ended without a verdict after both sides reached an out-of-court settlement. Zverev, who won the French and US Open in 2026, is alleged to have told French publication L'Equipe that: "I did everything I could, and my innocence has been proven.".

In a recent development, as Zverev's lawyers noted in a statement sent to DW: "The criminal proceedings were discontinued... without any finding of guilt, and the presumption of innocence remains unaffected.".

However, Zverev's statement has harmed Patea's standing and her career as an influencer, according to her lawyer, Michael Scheele.

In a recent development, "What she suffered after this interview in L'Equipe was published is nothing but a shitstorm. It's also detrimental to her business," Scheele told DW.

"We still don't know the truth objectively and we have an agreement in which he committed not to talk about the incident and the case at all," he added.

It has been revealed that however, in the statement sent to DW, Zverev's lawyers asserted that "there has been no breach of any contractual obligations or violation of Ms. Patea’s personality rights.".

Zverev had made similar comments before. On the day the settlement was reached, the tennis pro spoke to reporters at the 2024 French Open.

Industry observers note that "That's what dropping the case is: That is innocence. They're not going to drop the case if you're guilty at the end of the day," he noted.

The lawsuit, seen by DW, states that Zverev should be subject to "a fine of up to €250,000 ($275,000) to be determined for each instance of violation — and, in the event that such fine cannot be collected, substitute custodial detention of up to six months," should he be found guilty.

Zverev's lawyers reject the allegations.

"Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit. If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion protected by Article 5(1) of the German Basic Law," they said.

Industry observers note that "Our client would merely have expressed his personal conviction that he had done everything in his power to refute the allegations made against him and that he considers his innocence to have been confirmed by the outcome of the criminal proceedings. "He is fully entitled to hold and express this view.".

The law firm, Schertz Bergmann, added that: "Unlike the opposing counsel, we intend to conduct these proceedings in court rather than in the press.".

Scheele noted he and his client did not want to go back to court but were frustrated in their efforts to resolve matters in other ways.

According to recent reports, "We went forward writing to him in a polite way, asking him to sign and to declare that he's not going to repeat what he noted. And he didn't reply. So we wrote twice more, no reply.

Industry observers note that "That's when we had to decide to go to court, which was not the aim at the beginning. We wanted to avoid it, but we had no other choice.".

Zverev, now resident in Monaco, is currently playing in the season-ending ATP Finals tournament in Turin.

Latest Update: Kansas City Current's grit earns them spot in NWSL Championship while Gotham's logistics problems linger

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPCOMING YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune said post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

Icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game strategy that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during Fresh York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

"We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins said. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

It has been revealed that the introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness concerns over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

Sources indicate that "I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill mentioned. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

Sources indicate that in other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

Sources indicate that gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two important blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of Fresh York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

In the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

"As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas stated. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match plan that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

The Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

"Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a proposal," Armas said. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

Gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while currently headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

"Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros remarked. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

According to recent reports, more importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up plan for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull New York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

"I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce stated. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

According to recent reports, the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

"I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros noted. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

Industry observers note that "Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

Álex Baena opened the scoring in the 10th minute with a low, powerful shot from outside the area. It was his sixth LaLiga goal of the season. Johnny Cardoso doubled the lead on 30 minutes when David Soria missed a punch at a corner. It was Cardoso’s first league goal for Atlético.

England head coach Thomas Tuchel described his relationship with Jude Bellingham as being “in a good place” after admitting it had been “a bit up and down”.

Industry observers note that tuchel has two Bellinghams in his latest England squad after calling up Jude’s brother, Jobe, for the first time for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. If they play together, it will be the first time brothers have represented England in the same team since Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago.

This time last year, Tuchel cast doubt over Jude’s place in his team by picking Morgan Rogers over him, having not included the Real Madrid midfielder in an England squad the previous month.

But Jude performed superbly for Tuchel at the World Cup and was England’s best player during the last international camp. Tuchel revealed he has listened to his advice by calling up 21-year-old Jobe.

Asked if his relationship with Jude has developed, Tuchel said: “It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course, but we are in a good place.

“I love to be his coach, he’s a top player, a very influential player and it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable, he would not perform at that level.

Recent findings suggest that “At the moment, you see he’s happy to come into camp, he’s happy with the role he has, he’s fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them [Bellingham brothers] is just the next step. I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach.”.

Jobe has captained England’s Under-21s and, as well as U21 head coach Lee Carlsey, Tuchel acknowledged the influence of Jude on the Borussia Dortmund midfielder’s first senior call.

Jude once said that playing with Jobe for England would be “the biggest dream of my life” and that it would mean more to him than any trophies.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three days after tearing up as he confirmed his departure from the U.S.
  • After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity.
  • Industry observers note that "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he noted on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three days after tearing up as he confirmed his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino remarked he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

Industry observers note that "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he noted on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that indicates it's not important tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

It has been revealed that pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his intends for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

In a recent development, "What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the new coaches that arrive here," Pochettino remarked. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

For all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

In a recent development, for perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an important latest chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

Recent findings suggest that as for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his new role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

Sources indicate that two years removed from starting a new job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-important clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

According to recent reports, "For me, it's not difficult," he remarked of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most important [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are presently in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

Villarreal visit Slavia Prague after seven straight Champions League away defeats, a record for a Spanish club. Their hosts have gone 23 games without a win in the competition, so one of the two runs must end today.

Villarreal face Slavia Prague in the Champions League today carrying a losing run that UEFA indicates is a record for a Spanish club. They have lost each of their last seven away games in the competition. Their hosts carry a burden of their own. Slavia have eight draws and 15 defeats in their last 23 Champions League games. That run equals the competition’s worst, set by Steaua București between 2006 and 2013.

According to recent reports, one of the two sequences has to end. A Slavia win would end their drought. Any other result would stop Villarreal’s run of away defeats. Kick-off is at 17:45 GMT.

That single win was a 3-1 home victory over Napoli on 13 October. The rest of the league phase has gone badly. Villarreal lost 3-2 at Borussia Dortmund on 8 September and 4-3 at Liverpool on 20 October. PSG then won 6-0 at La Cerámica on 3 November.

In a recent development, that leaves Villarreal 29th with three points. Another defeat would leave them close to elimination with three games to play.

Industry observers note that the defence is the clearest problem. Villarreal have not kept a clean sheet in any of those 15 games, a club record. None of their last 35 games in the Champions League proper has ended goalless.

Falling behind early has also been fatal. Villarreal have never won a Champions League game when trailing at half-time, with two draws and 13 defeats. On eight occasions they have gone into the interval losing on the road, and every one of those matches ended in defeat.

Nathan Saliba, Juan Foyth and Ilias Akhomach are all missing in Prague, EFE reported. Gerard Moreno trained before the game and could return.

In a recent development, trpišovský has six draws and 12 defeats from his 19 Champions League matches, all in charge of Slavia. UEFA describes that as the longest winless run of any coach in the competition. Slavia have also never beaten a Spanish club from the group or league phase onwards, with two draws and four defeats. The two clubs have not met since their two games in 2017.

Villarreal coach Iñigo Pérez still expects a hard night. Speaking in Prague, he stated no team in the Champions League is as aggressive as Slavia. He called the game “transcendental” for how the league phase plays out. He added that the city’s cold weather would not be an excuse.

It has been revealed that defender Sergi Cardona said the team must learn last season’s lesson. He expects the game to be extremely demanding.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our guts contain around 40 trillion bacterial cells, a similar quantity to the number of cells in the entire human body1. Although the community of bacterial species in the human gut usually stays relatively stable over time2, genetic mutations in such bacteria can be associated with a measure of body size called the body mass index3. Writing in Nature, Wang et al.4 scanned the gut bacteria of some 10,000 people for genetic variation and searched for statistically significant associations with almost 250 characteristics, including age, height and cardiovascular fitness. The authors singled out one adaptation that seems to help one of the most abundant bacterial species in the human gut to resist a form of stress called oxidative stress, which damages cells and increases as people age.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that historically, goalkeeper has been a position of strength for the United States men's national team, to the extent that during the time of Tim Howard and Brad Guzan, both were playing Premier League soccer, but only one could start between the sticks.
  • During Mauricio Pochettino's tenure, Matt Freese has been his starting keeper, taking over during the Gold Cup and starting every game that he was available for until the September/October international window, when Pochettino used Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake.
  • Following that match, Kochen acknowledged that the USMNT squad has done a lot to put him in this position, and he'll know that even if Pochettino won't be the manager choosing the lineups, performances like this one will be important for how the USMNT keeper picture looks moving forward.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that historically, goalkeeper has been a position of strength for the United States men's national team, to the extent that during the time of Tim Howard and Brad Guzan, both were playing Premier League soccer, but only one could start between the sticks. Things have changed since then, with numerous keepers coming through the ranks over the years, with most playing domestically or sitting on the bench for stronger European sides. However, that could be coming to an end for the team.

During Mauricio Pochettino's tenure, Matt Freese has been his starting keeper, taking over during the Gold Cup and starting every game that he was available for until the September/October international window, when Pochettino used Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake. Kochen, who is playing his first season of first-team soccer at Lyngby in Denmark (where center back Neil Pierre also got his first taste of senior soccer), got the clean sheet against Mexico during that camp and turned that into a start against Haiti in Concacaf Nations League play in his native Miami, setting the USMNT up well to advance to the semifinals of the tournament.

Following that match, Kochen acknowledged that the USMNT squad has done a lot to put him in this position, and he'll know that even if Pochettino won't be the manager choosing the lineups, performances like this one will be important for how the USMNT keeper picture looks moving forward.

"I feel like I've grown quite a lot," Kochen said following the match, reflecting on his adjustment to the national team. "I'm getting used to competing at the international level, but I've just got to give it to my team because they've been unbelievable. They make it so easy to just come out here and play free and be me, so without them, this wouldn't be possible.".

His growth is evident; one of the first things that comes to mind when watching the 20-year-old is his poise. Kochen had the ball at his feet plenty, completing all 20 of his passes to help send the attack on its way, and also made the two saves that he needed to on a mostly quiet night. His age also showed when Haiti scored with him out of position, a goal that was called back for offside, but you take the good with the bad for young players because that's a learning moment, and as he earns more reps at the senior level, those are the kind of mistakes that can be ironed out.

"I'm not saying he hasn't played games in Barcelona, but at the senior level, every game he plays, he gets better and better and better," one of Kochen's coaches, Andreas Bjelland, told CBS Sports. "Because understanding the full-pitch play, and not only being on the line, just taking shots, and being a training goalie, but now he's playing for points every week. He's growing as a player, as a person, and as somebody we can trust more and more in the stuff we do. So it's nice to see that it has come to this ... It's quite impressive.".

Industry observers note that you can't teach poise, and spending more than five years in the Barcelona system highlights in how Kochen carries himself. It's becoming more common in American soccer for young players to test themselves abroad or to get into Major League Soccer teams at a younger age, and when they succeed, it goes a long way developmentally, as Kochen's case shows.

"He is a person who trusts himself a lot. That's also why he's a good goalie, that at such a young age he hasn't that massive of a doubt of himself," Mikkel Jespersen, Lyngby's other coach noted. "He knows what he's capable of doing, and that's really important as a goalie: that you trust yourself and know what things you are doing is something that can succeed in a longer period.".

In a recent development, while it's unknown what the next USMNT manager will value in a keeper, being able to perform in an uncertain environment with your coach having one foot out the door is something that will go a long way for Kochen's chances. In keeper terms, Kochen has plenty of time ahead of him, as players at his position regularly play until their late 30s or early 40s, so if he can continue this trajectory, the question of who protects the net could be solved for the foreseeable future.

Of course, that's a lot of projecting, but when the next generation of the USMNT is developing at an astounding rate, it's only natural to think about where players like Kochen could end up. Doing this in only his first season of professional soccer is already impressive, but the best is yet to come.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares of US artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic saw their first day of trading on Thursday on the US tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange.

Anthropic is one of the global leaders in AI technology and is best known for its Claude chatbot.

In a recent development, the stock opened at $111.50 (€101.7) — that's 34% higher than the IPO price of $83 and puts the firm's valuation at $2 trillion. Anthropic stock ended the first day of trading at $97 per share.

The tech giant's share performance is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

The San Francisco-based tech giant behind the Claude AI tool has offered 980 million shares at $83 per share, raising a record $81 billion.

This valued the firm at $1.5 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that anthropic is the first significant AI manufacturer to go public. Its main competitor, ChatGPT-maker OpenAI,  has reportedly pushed its IPO to 2027.

Issuing shares on the stock market is essentially a way to raise money and avoid taking on debt.

Anthropic has already taken on $6.2 billion in debt and is not yet making a profit. At the same time, it faces massive bills for computer power and data centers.

That specific financial situation is one of the reasons for persistent concern that the AI boom might be a bubble that will eventually burst.

After four matchdays, the league phase has been whittled down to only two games left for each of the 18 clubs, and the margin between a bye into the quarterfinals and an extra round of knockout playoffs in February will come down to dwindling points.

According to recent reports, OL Lyonnes rule the league phase at the moment. They top the tournament table with ten points, level with FC Barcelona but with a superior goal difference. Just behind the two Champions League contenders are Bayern Munich and Arsenal, with Chelsea FC and Manchester City creeping closer to the top four. Out of the 18 clubs competing, only four will earn direct berths to the quarterfinals, and eight will compete for a future spot alongside them.

The final six clubs with the least amount of points will see their Champions League dream end, so matchday 5 will be a crucial turning point for several teams.

In a recent development, fighting for top spot positioning will be Arsenal and OL Lyonnes, and Chelsea against Paris Saint-Germain. HB Koge, Roma, and tournament debutants Inter Milan are level on four points and need to be in full urgency mode if they're to leapfrog and remain in contention for future rounds.

How Emile Heskey fell into a sketchy world peddling controversial drugs: From England star worth £12m to bankruptcy, unpaid tax and a bitter divorce

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 07:35 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Emile Heskey is standing in a warehouse, dressed in a black adidas tracksuit, trying to sell you a jar of curious sweet treats.
  • He smiles into the camera with the gentle-giant warmth that characterised his football career – but Heskey is in unfamiliar territory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 07:35 EST, 26 November 2026.

Emile Heskey is standing in a warehouse, dressed in a black adidas tracksuit, trying to sell you a jar of curious sweet treats.

He smiles into the camera with the gentle-giant warmth that characterised his football career – but Heskey is in unfamiliar territory.

Behind him, stacked on shelf after shelf, are containers full of Supreme CBD gummies.

The man who scored in England's 5-1 thrashing of Germany in 2001, who scored 110 Premier League goals for Leicester, Liverpool, Birmingham, Wigan and Aston Villa plus seven more for his country, is, remarkably, trying to flog you an assortment of products containing cannabidiol, a legal but controversial ingredient derived from cannabis.

Today, he is promoting a tub of CBD strawberry gummies, as well as oil. If you fancy an exclusive discount, there's a special code bearing his name.

‘I swear by these products for my sleep,’ he writes in the caption on Instagram. ‘They have been fantastic for me for years now!’.

Emile Heskey spends his days trying to flog controversial Supreme CBD products (Instagram: theemileheskey).

He is one of multiple former footballers promoting the products for ex-Olympic boxer Anthony Fowler - despite their illegal claims about the supposed health benefits.

According to recent reports, heskey, 48, was once one of English football's most respected players. He won 62 caps for England, appearing at two World Cups. He won five trophies at Liverpool and two League Cups at Leicester.

Occasionally mocked for his lack of goals – he averaged roughly one every five games during his club career – he carried himself with humour and grace. Since retiring, his reputation has helped him secure roles with England's youth pathway and Leicester's women's team, as well as occasional punditry work for the BBC.

Sources indicate that in September, he scored in an England legends match against Poland, playing alongside John Terry and Robbie Fowler. This month, he was a guest of honour at Liverpool's Anfield VIP Experience. He remains a regular on the speakers' circuit, with more appearances booked before Christmas.

All of which begs the question: what is he doing promoting Supreme CBD? Why is he filming several videos a month for a tech giant with such a troubled regulatory record?

Where once he shared a dressing room with Steven Gerrard and David Beckham, he now shares an ambassadorial roster with Katie Price.

It is unclear whether Heskey is aware of the concerns surrounding Supreme CBD products, or the repeated occasions on which the company has fallen foul of advertising rules.

Its founder, Anthony Fowler, a former Team GB Olympic boxer, has made unsubstantiated claims that his cannabidiol products can help treat mental health conditions and autism in children.

There is likely a financial incentive for Heskey, although the terms of any arrangement are unclear. Equally, he appears genuinely convinced of the products' benefits. He claims the oil has done wonders for his sleep and eased his aches and pains.

Heskey's wife Chantelle has issued divorce proceedings - and claims he cancelled a holiday with their kids to go away with his newly introduced partner instead.

Heskey and his fresh partner Jade Slusarczyk spent two weeks together in Cyprus and Greece.

Chantelle branded Heskey 'vile' and claimed he deleted her comment on an Instagram post about the upcoming couple's holiday.

Recent findings suggest that that may well be true. The NHS acknowledges that CBD has some medical uses, but warns that the ‘quality and content’ of products sold online can be uncertain and that they ‘may be illegal and potentially dangerous’. Nor is there any guarantee that products sold in health stores will be of ‘good quality’.

It has been revealed that supreme CBD have repeatedly breached advertising rules. In June, the Advertising Standards Authority took action over the firm's continued use of prohibited claims that CBD could treat, prevent or cure human disease.

The regulator has also upheld complaints about celebrity promotions that failed to make clear they were advertisements.

Recent findings suggest that supreme CBD have made claims that their products can treat anxiety, insomnia and depression. Such medicinal claims are prohibited in advertising for products that have not been authorised as medicines. It is uncomfortable ground for Heskey to find himself on.

Sources indicate that last year, Fowler also spoke about refusing chemotherapy for his two-year-old daughter's tumour, claiming CBD oil had had a 'massive' effect on it instead. Price, a paid brand ambassador, amplified those claims on her own social media channels, including posted to her 1.6million followers on X that the tumour had 'shrunk' as a result.

British medical and food safety authorities advise that CBD should not be given to those under the age of 18.

CBD can also affect how other medicines work, meaning anyone using it alongside other treatments should seek medical advice. Certain medicinal CBD treatments require regular monitoring because of their potential effects on the liver.

Sources indicate that it is not unusual for former sportspeople to struggle with insomnia, depression or persistent pain after retirement. It has been revealed that good morning and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Leeds United and Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road. The home side, lions at night and mice in the morning, have the unenviable record of 21 top-flight matches with a kick-off time before 3pm without a win. All that extra TV moolah comes in handy but their home ground, a bearpit under the floodlights, is neutered when its denizens are yawning instead of being fired up by social lubricant.

Daniel Farke’s team started the campaign well but are now without a win in five, drawing three matches with teams beneath them in the table – Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Sunderland – and  losing to two above them, Arsenal and Bournemouth. In fairness they played well against the champions for an hour and were deservedly in the lead until Mikel Arteta turnd to his billionaire’s bench and changed the game. At Bournemouth last week they also made a decent start, had a goal disallowed for striking Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s arm and then James Trafford chucked one in.

They never recovered, found themselves increasingly bogged down when trying to unlock a low block and were mugged on the break in added time to lose 2-0. They are a robust side overly reliant on their wing-backs to create chances for their No 9 in the absence of the injured Noah Okafor who was unavailable to train with the team this week because of a groin injury but may be fit enough for the bench.

In a recent development, spurs, by contrast, are buoyant following three wins on the bounce – over Coventry, Chelsea and Palace, two with clean sheets – that has taken them from 19th to ninth, three places above Leeds. They have won their last three visits to Elland Road, 0-4 under Antonio Conte, which proved to be the last match of Marcelo Bielsa’s glorious spell at the Peacocks, 1-4 under Ryan Mason, which sealed Leeds’ relegation, and 1-2 under Tomas Frank last year by virtue of goals from Mathys Tel and Mohammed Kudus as the home side struggled against their width back in the days before their switch to a back three.

Tel also scored in Spurs’ home game, a 1-1 draw in May, and then kicked Ethan Ampadu in the head to concede the penalty from which Leeds equalised. I wonder what kind of impact he will have today. Incidentally Roberto De Zerbi on his last visit to Leeds when manager of Brighton in 2022-23 had such a strop on the touchline when the home team equalised that he was within a gnat’s whisker of being sent off.

In one of the most daring collaborations of recent years, adidas has joined forces with Japanese streetwear powerhouse BAPE to create a football collection that fuses pitch performance with high-octane style.

The collection is led by two standout football boots: the Predator Elite FT Firm Ground and the F50 Elite Firm Ground.

The Predator Elite, instantly recognisable for its fold-over tongue, is reimagined in BAPEâs signature green ABC CAMO with gold stripes, a shark graphic on the lteral, alternating gold logos on the tongues, and ABC CAMO sockliners.

Meanwhile, the F50 Elite features a striking blue-to-pink gradient ABC CAMO upper, shark graphic on the medial, and clear star prints across the surface. Both pairs are showstoppers built to turn heads on and off the pitch.

Beyond the boots, the collaboration extends to footwear and apparel, including reimagined adidas Sambas with a BABY MILO skull face in rubber, ABC CAMO jerseys, shorts, tights, and a BABY MILO football tee.

Accessories complete the set, with an ABC CAMO duffle bag and a BABY MILO shoulder bag rounding out the collection.

Fronted by Real Madrid and Brazil legend Marcelo, known for his flair on and off the pitch, the 'adidas x BAPE' football collection is a truly global statement piece, appealing to fashion fans and football enthusiasts from Asia to the Americas and Europe.

The collection drops September 6th via Confirmed, adidas.com, select adidas retail partners, BAPE.com, and BAPE STORE locations worldwide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in a farewell for Mauricio Pochettino before he heads to Manchester United, the United States men's national team were able to defeat Haiti 2-0 on Tuesday night, advancing in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals 8-0 on aggregate. Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a bicycle-kick goal to kick things off, which was the emphatic send-off that was needed prior to Pochettino arriving in Manchester, but the USMNT were able to keep things up in the celebration in Cincinnati.

CHRISTIAN PULISIC GET ON YOUR BIKE‼️#USMNT x @VW pic.twitter.com/Yb3yqXfC33.

It has been revealed that julian Hall followed with a poacher's goal as Weston McKennie played orchestrator, and it continued a theme that whoever ends up taking over the national team will have tough decisions ahead. Folarin Balogun is struggling for minutes with Monaco and is looking to make a move at the end of the season, and Hall has done everything that he can to increase his own standing with five goals in six games for the USMNT.

The Latest York Red Bulls star has a ways to go considering that he's still only 18 and will need to gain experience against top teams in the world instead of just Haiti, but he also can't ask for a better start than what he has gotten off to. It's why this is such an attractive job for whoever takes over the USMNT. They'll be able to build upon the good that Pochettino has instilled; the talent is there to move the squad forward, and there's plenty to love about the youth of the USMNT.

It has been revealed that and alongside that, Pulisic has essentially screamed don't forget about me. During this camp, the Milan man has followed up on signing a latest contract with the club by reaching 35 national team goals, moving into fourth all time for the USMNT over Eric Wynalda. Diego Kochen added to the good vibes with a third straight clean sheet, and Neil Pierre was even able to be cap-tied against the nation that he's also eligible for as the full-circle moments were left and right.

Pulisic, the former 17-year-old phenom, was subbed off for Cavan Sullivan, the current 17-year-old phenom, and while the goal difference may have been larger in the first leg between these sides, this felt like a more measured performance despite the strangeness of Pochettino's assistants heading to United while he managed the squad prior to catching his own charter.

This camp had every chance of being a disaster given the circumstances of Pochettino leaving, but all parties did what was needed during this camp. All dual nationals were capped, including Santiago Castaneda, showing that even on his way out, Pochettino made sure to take care of the future of the federation. On to the next round of the Concacaf Nations League with a new manager and no complaints with the performance so far for the squad.

Celta Vigo lost at home to Bournemouth even though the visitors played most of the game a man down. The defeat extends a difficult run for Claudio Giráldez's side, while the visitors moved to the top of the Europa League table.

Bournemouth came from behind to beat Celta Vigo 1-2 at the Municipal de Balaídos on Thursday 26 November 2026. With Javier Rueda García providing the assist for Aspas, Celta went into the break 1-0 up.

The game turned soon after the restart. Álvaro Rodríguez, the Uruguay international, headed Bournemouth level in the 47th minute from an Amine Adli assist. Rayan then scored the winner on a counter-attack in the 78th minute, set up by Marcus Tavernier. Aspas was booked for dissent in the same minute.

Industry observers note that the match statistics show how much of the play Celta had. The hosts completed 527 passes from 607. Bournemouth completed 264 from 333. Fourteen of Celta’s attempts came from inside the box, against four for the visitors.

Celta’s finishing did not match that volume. They put five shots on target, while Bournemouth managed six. Seven Celta efforts were blocked and eight went wide. Celta goalkeeper Ionuț Radu made four saves.

Industry observers note that giráldez told EFE that his team did not show enough composure or intelligence to make use of the extra man after Diakité’s dismissal. In his view, Rodríguez’s equaliser brought back the anxiety of Celta’s poor run.

According to recent reports, that run is visible in the results. Celta have won one of their last six games in all competitions, a 5-0 victory over Salamanca UDS. Before Bournemouth, they lost 1-2 to Real Madrid. They also drew 0-0 with Levante and lost to Union St. Gilloise and Rayo Vallecano.

Bournemouth’s recent run includes victories over Nottingham Forest, Ipswich, Leeds and Aston Villa.

According to recent reports, the 2026/27 Europa League is the club’s debut in European competition. Before Vigo, they had beaten Real Sociedad, Sturm Graz, AC Milan and Sparta Praha in the competition. Rodríguez was the top-rated player in the match, with a rating of 7.9.

Play was brought to a standstill during Austriaâs 2026 World Cup qualifier against Cyprus after a sinkhole suddenly appeared on the pitch late in the second half.

The bizarre incident occurred around the 75th minute, when Danish referee Jakob Kehlet halted the match after noticing the gaping hole near Austria keeper Alexander Schlagerâs box at the Raiffeisen Arena, in Linz.

The opening was wide enough to swallow an entire football, prompting ground staff to rush on with buckets of sand in a frantic attempt to patch it up.

After more than seven minutes of repairs, Kehlet finally gave the green light to resume, with Austria eventually sealing a 1-0 win thanks to Marcel Sabitzerâs second-half penalty â scored before the ground gave way.

The win means Austria are now second in Group H qualifying, having won all three of their games so far, behind also unbeaten Bosnia and Herzegovina.

#220452. USWNT roster for Concacaf W Championship: Ashley Sanchez back, Sam Coffey returns, and Naomi Girma misses out

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1333 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

USWNT roster for Concacaf W Championship: Ashley Sanchez back, Sam Coffey returns, and Naomi Girma misses out

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1333 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest roster of the year for the U.S.
  • The tournament serves as the World Cup qualifiers, and four teams will earn spots in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, with future Olympic spots also in play.
  • In just nine short days, eight teams will compete in a quarterfinal round.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest roster of the year for the U.S. women's national team is here. Head coach Emma Hayes has named a 23-player roster for the upcoming 2026 Concacaf W Championship.

The tournament serves as the World Cup qualifiers, and four teams will earn spots in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, with future Olympic spots also in play. Fans can watch all the Concacaf W Championship matches on Paramount+.

In just nine short days, eight teams will compete in a quarterfinal round. The U.S. and Canada earned direct byes into the tournament as Concacaf's top two ranked teams, and six teams now join them after a preliminary qualifying round. The USWNT will face El Salvador on Nov. 27 in the quarterfinal round, and if they advance, they'll clinch a spot in next year's World Cup. The other matchups are Canada against Panama, Mexico vs. Haiti, and Jamaica will play Costa Rica.

"It's been a great year of growth and learning for our team, and for a long time the focus has been on qualifying for the World Cup, so now that time has arrived," said Hayes.

In a recent development, "I want to see relentless consistency from our players, individually and as a team, and I want us to be elite in both penalty boxes. If we can achieve that, I'm confident those performances will carry us through to meet our standards and goals. This is my first Concacaf event and the first for many of our players, so we're all looking forward to the experience.".

Sources indicate that hayes selected a full roster that features several players competing in their first-ever senior-level World Cup qualifying tournament, and a handful of veterans. Just eight of the 23 players selected were members of the 2022 Concacaf W Championship roster: forwards Mallory Swanson, Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson, and Ashley Sanchez; defender Emily Fox; and midfielders Lindsey Heaps, Rose Lavelle, and Sam Coffey -- who joined mid-tournament that year.

Coffey returns to the roster after missing two previous international windows while managing a lower-leg injury. Defender Naomi Girma is out as she continues to manage a lingering calf injury. The centerback has not featured with the national team since April, and has yet to play with Chelsea FC this season. Midfielder Olivia Moultrie is currently rehabbing from an ACL injury sustained in August. Other notable omissions on the roster are Jaedyn Shaw and Ally Sentnor, both of whom have been part of U23 and senior camps throughout the year.

This is just the third camp for the attacking line of "triple espresso" since the 2024 Olympics. If the trio starts a match during the Concacaf W Championship, it will be the first time they start a game together since the gold medal match. Both Swanson and Wilson have worked their way back into senior camps over the year following maternity leave.

Listed by position (club; caps/goals).

Goalkeepers (3): Claudia Dickey (Seattle Reign FC; 12/0), Mandy McGlynn (Utah Royals FC; 6/0), Phallon Tullis-Joyce (Manchester United, ENG; 8/0).

Defenders (8): Tierna Davidson (Gotham FC; 72/3), Kate Del Fava (Utah Royals FC; 1/0), Emily Fox (Arsenal FC, ENG; 80/1), Avery Patterson (Houston Dash; 15/1), Tara Rudd (Washington Spirit; 12/0), Evelyn Shores (Angel City FC; 0/0), Gisele Thompson (Angel City FC; 12/0), Kennedy Wesley (San Diego Wave FC; 9/1).

Midfielders (6): Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current; 7/1), Sam Coffey (Manchester City, ENG; 46/5), Lindsey Heaps (Denver Summit FC; 180/40), Claire Hutton (Bay FC; 22/1), Rose Lavelle (Gotham FC; 124/29), Lily Yohannes (OL Lyonnes, FRA; 22/1).

Forwards (6): Michelle Cooper (Kansas City Current; 16/1), Trinity Rodman (Washington Spirit; 59/13), Ashley Sanchez (North Carolina Courage; 30/4), Mallory Swanson (Chicago Stars; 105/39), Alyssa Thompson (Chelsea FC, ENG; 34/4), Sophia Wilson (Portland Thorns FC; 65/25).

Ashley Sanchez's return to the roster comes after standout performances against Spain last window and a stellar 2026 NWSL regular season where she won the Golden Boot with 20 goals scored. She was also nominated for the 2026 NWSL MVP award. A positional shift to left winger and an outrageous amount of scoring have all led her back to the USWNT due to consistent performances, a key factor for Hayes with her large player pool.

According to recent reports, "Be consistent first of all in performance. Ashley Sanchez wasn't on our radar, not because she isn't talented, but there were certain things we demanded from the performance that I think she has delivered in her game on a regular basis. So, I think that's the first thing. I think you've seen that includes Croix Bethune coming into this camp -- been outstanding in the number 10 position all year, and would have been in last camp as well if she was fit. You do have to consistently find consistent performances, particularly if you're a player that doesn't have credit in the bank," Hayes said.

Recent findings suggest that as the World Cup gets nearer, finalizing a roster for the 2027 summer tournament is even closer. Things like consistent form and senior-level experience will come into play when naming a final 23 for the World Cup for Hayes.

Recent findings suggest that "If you're a Mallory Swanson and delivered on a world stage on a regular basis for the national team, it does alter things slightly. No, we don't want players that are in our group that are in a place where they're not fighting to improve every day or be as competitive as they could possibly be, but I think when players have stacked and accumulated a lot of experience over a period of time, that is always going to put them in a steady position," Hayes explained.

"But it doesn't guarantee anything. I will be unafraid to leave anybody off that plane if I don't feel that they are applying themselves to put ourselves in the best possible position to compete. Which is why this upcoming camp, our job is to qualify for the World Cup, and so everything we have worked towards is ensuring that every player that comes in at camp makes sure they lift their level and they position the team to have the most positive outcome, regardless of the opponent. And I'd be demanding as much as I always do, but I have a big expectation from our senior players to step up.".

Industry observers note that el Salvador is the eighth-ranked team in the Concacaf W Championship and earned its spot following a preliminary qualifying round. The group is coached by manager Eric Acuña, who recently made headlines for harshly criticizing his players in a press conference following losses to Paraguay last month.

Still, Hayes and the staff aren't taking any opponent lightly no matter the rankings or state of the locker room.

"It's a team that knows is competing for something, so it doesn't matter the opponent; they're competing to go to a World Cup, and do I think that will be it will be demanding and taxing? And yes, I do. In many different ways, because the expectations are all on us. I think for them, it's how are they going to disrupt us and make it difficult? But they have two players in the front line that can cause a lot of problems, particularly in transition. So we have to set up for that," Hayes noted.

"I think when it when it comes to the players, I've always championed creating positive environments for players. And yeah, I'm sad for the players to hear what they've gone through, but as always, I can't control that. I want the best for players all of the time in their environments, but I am here to represent the U.S. and try and help us qualify for the World Cup. So my focus is on that. Even if my heart goes out to the players and I think we still have a lot of work to do in the women's game to keep driving female-centered, female-lens environments where women can thrive.".

#220446. Breaking: Why U.S. Soccer's move to name Emma Hayes to the USMNT hiring committee makes sense

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1993 w)
